UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_41_Content:
To anyone who finds this sheet of paper. Know that I was not a bad person. I was just a survivor.

It has been almost a year since the outbreak occurred. I had to do things I'm not proud of to survive. Abandoned family, friends, and strangers of all kinds. Living in this apartment complex, I managed to stock up on supplies to the point that they are filling up my bedroom with things I've been collecting. Often, when I get out to scavenge at night, I can see those zombies just pacing about. I know, zombies-how cliche. But hey, this is the real deal. It has happened here in Kentucky, of all places! Why do I only go out at night? Because it seems to be safest from both people and zombies. As those things can't be clearly seen when it is completely dark. However, their sense of hearing is quite frightening.

Often, I find groups of other survivors here in Louisville. All with the same goal in mind: to survive. Some are good, and some are just plain horrible.

One night, I had no choice. It wasn't my fault; I know I shouldn't have, but I had no choice! I was stupid enough to infiltrate another group's stash house. because I thought they weren't home. This group isn't the greatest of people or the brightest. They often harass or, on rare occasions, kill other survivors for their supplies. Anyway, here I was, inside, and I managed to picklock their backdoor with ease. It was dark; that's smart. They kept their lights off. However, my eyesight is fair in the dark. A few doors down, I found their stash, and I packed up what I could take with me. Make sure everything is as it should be. I lock the door as if no one has ever passed by. That was when I heard someone crying at the door next to their stash. I opened it, and inside was a woman who was chained to a pipe. She notices me and begins to panic. I do my best to calm her down. However, I heard gunshots downstairs and something along the lines of "Shit, they're insidious, Carl, get the fucking guns, man!", I knew then that the zombies had gotten inside their safe place. I couldn't free the woman. I had nothing on me, and I knew I had little time on my hands. With little to no choice, I chose to stay alive and safe. I apologized to her and closed the door, muffling her screams.

I ran back home.

Now, most of you will think of me as a suicidal monster. The world has gone to shit; everyone is out for themselves. Why should I care what others think? I want to survive. By any means necessary.

A couple of days ago, I had to kill a teenage boy. Because he had spotted me looting a vehicle from another group. He was about to alarm his group when I stabbed him straight through his windpipe with my makeshift wooden spear. I did not hesitate, nor did I care. I needed to survive and wasn't going to let some little shit be the end of me. However, another set of eyes witnessed what I had done and screamed for help. A pack of wolves was soon upon me, a mere rat in their eyes. Luckily, I had some grenades I managed to snatch from a military vehicle a night ago. I removed the pins from a few of them and threatened to go with everyone. They couldn't see my face as It was covered with a bandana. So all they did was shout out names like "Damn filthy rat!". Let's just say I ended up leaving alive that day.

Little did I know that the boy's death would come back to haunt me.
Literally.

(Bloody footprints are covering some of the words but are still readable.)
because I sit here now. Writing this.
This morning, I thought of looting in broad daylight. A huge mistake, I know. A rat going out in the morning instead of the night. That same group was looting one of my favorite hotels for supplies. I snuck up behind one of them and slit their throat. It was a young woman. The others had left already, it seemed to me. So I began to loot the place and her body. Who the fuck knew that these freaks would carry around their dead like pets? This undead motherfucker snuck up behind me, taking a chunk from my neck. It was the kid that I had killed days ago.

Shit luck, am I right? Well, I know I won't live long now. Well, at least the next set of survivors that find my place will have something. Leaving my stash behind.
Don't bother looking for me. I'll be long dead if I'm going to die. I'll die with those fuckers; I know where they eat and shit.

Tip to future survivors Don't get cocky like I did. It will cost you.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_42_Content:
Attention survivor,
If you are reading this, it means you are still alive amidst this Hell. I write this note to warn you about the Knox Event and its sinister origins. SPIFFCO, the restaurant chain, is the root cause of this nightmare. Their establishments have been spreading a mysterious illness, turning people into the undead horrors that now roam the streets.

I fear that I too have fallen victim to their vile scheme. The food they claim is beef seems far from it, and I suspect there's something much darker hidden within their meals. It is crucial to avoid consuming anything from SPIFFCO if you wish to stay alive and uninfected.

Stay vigilant and trust no one. The world we once knew has become a living nightmare, and the only way to survive is to remain cautious and resourceful. If you encounter others, be careful whom you trust, as the virus may have already taken hold of them.

We must find a way to fight back against this darkness and restore humanity. Share this warning with anyone you can, as information may be our greatest weapon against this zombie apocalypse.
Stay strong and keep hope alive.

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_44_Content:
Uncle Bob, the phone lines are still down, so it's just letters from me for the time being. Just wanted to let you know that I'm okay, despite everything that's been going down these past few days. I normally wouldn't have this much time to write, but our wing's on lockdown today. Can't separate the truth from the con talk these days, but what I do know is some sicko was caught eating his cellmate. We all saw the guy, covered in blood and grayer than the cold, hard concrete beneath our toes, getting wheeled out by the COs strapped to those chairs that they put Hannibal Lecter in. Yeah, straight out of the Silence of the Lambs movie, mask and all. I didn't know they actually had stuff like that! If he ever leaves the hole, which I sure as hell hope he doesn't, he'll be taking the nickname "Hannibal the Cannibal" to his grave. At least I have my trial date coming up this Friday; maybe the appeal will finally go through and you and I will get to hang out and go fishing again like the good old days. They keep delaying it, though, probably because of this new bug everyone's so afraid of now. I think it's another one of those bird flu things they sometimes talk about on TV; it's bad enough that they've
even got the army enforcing a quarantine around all of Knox County. Some cons in here are swearing on their own mothers that they knew so-and-so who caught this mystery bug, and that now they're in and out the infirmary running a really nasty fever. I wish they were lying, but more and more guys in here have been getting sick lately. Even a few COs are clocking out early saying they've got the "Knox bug". And you won't believe the kind of rumors this one nutjob is spreading around here about it. The guy's saying old Hannibal had the bug before anybody else, and that it's what caused him to lose his marbles and do what he did to his poor celly, like rabies or something. He rants on and on all night about how everyone who catches the bug is a ticking time bomb, and it's only a matter of time before we're all just like Hannibal the Cannibal. I told him he needed to stop taking everything he heard on KnoxTalk radio as the gospel of truth, and to zip it before someone less kind than myself landed him in the very same infirmary bed that all the sick folks are coughing, barfing, and vomiting all over. That sure as hell shut him up.

It's been four or five hours now, and the lockdown still hasn't been lifted. Apparently it's just our cell block anymore, but a total lockdown. Whatever's happening, I just hope the COs at least have the decency to serve us our lunches. Rumors are spreading wild now, and not just from the nutty guy. It seems everyone's got their own idea of why we're still on lockdown, and half of them are hiding under their pillows thinking that Hannibal broke loose and is coming back for seconds. You remember my cellmate, Hugh, the guy who does janitorial work around the jail? I've known Hugh going on for half a year, and he's not one to spout fairytales. He says he was mopping up when a CO, white like she'd seen the boogeyman, ran over and snatched the broomstick right out of his hands before hauling on back the way she came and jabbing it in between the handles of the canteen doors just before a whole lot of hands started banging on them from the other side. Hugh said that was about an hour before the lockdown started; he thinks somebody started a riot in there, and that's what's causing all this. Causing everybody else to miss their breakfast; selfish pricks. Poor Hugh's sick now, too; I just hope it's his seasonal allergies, and not that bug he's got. I'm going to try to get some shut eye. So damn anxious, though. This is going to be a long night. I hope this whole clusterfuck doesn't make me miss my court date.

Hey shit head. You know you who are. It's me, Bill Benson. Remember how we promised each other, that we'd ride this out together? That we'd have each other's backs no matter what, and we'd never abandon one another regardless of how fucking bad it got, no matter how terrifying the situation?

You lied.

You know exactly what you fucking did. You thought you could make off with ALL of our food, all of MY fucking ammo-- you didn't do ANY of the fucking preparation, "roomie". You always tried to poke fun at me, make me out like I was paranoid, even fucking called the cops because you were so fucking scared shitless that I was exercising my right to keep and bear arms. Lo and fucking behold, the dead walk the earth, yea the apocalypse is nigh, and you think you can just take all my shit, cut and run? After I taught you to shoot, after I bared my heart and soul to you, after the things we did together? You think you can just fucking GET AWAY with it?

You are unbelievably stupid. You fired off a shot, knowing damn well it'd bring a herd of those fuckers down onto the apartment, and you stole my god damn truck, and now I'm getting REALLY close to finding you. UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_49_Content:
The nasty girls are shooting on sight now. They're not even bothering to hide it anymore, anyone trying to leave, or trying to enter, gets shot dead. Used to be they'd just arrest you, quarantine you then let you go into the city to evac, that's what my sister said on the radio before she and a few dozen others got ferried across the river into Indiana.

I write this letter to anybody who might find it from my deathbed. Me and my cousin Jesse tried to approach the gate, wanting to get in, to evacuate like everyone else, but the moment we came into sight, they killed Jesse, blew his brains out all over the concrete with an M16, and then they popped me a few times.

I managed to get away, to get back to my car, but I'm losing blood just steady enough that I've got maybe twenty minutes left as I write this. My last will and testament to whoever comes across this letter, praying it hasn't been soaked through:

You can have all my gear. I won't be needing it. If you're able and willing, try to get to Indianapolis, that's where they took my sister Vivian. Give her this note, so she's not left in the dark.

I love you Viv.

Mitchell

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_6_Content:
Day 28... It has been quiet since the end of the first week as the rotten walking corpse roams the earth. These things seem to appear more and more every day, bigger and bigger in number all around the place... I need to set up a perimeter around Riverside now.

I have been outside of Riverside town to explore the region, and ran into a lot of what's left of the old world... It's just the same everywhere, no survivors, just the world and me and the undead.

I also stopped by at the army quarter by South East of Rosewood as well and of course, nothing but one military personnel who got left behind. They seemed to be in a hurry and left their stuff behind including their vehicle and equipment that I can use... I'm going to need it.
When I was driving out to get back onto the highway I heard it, a military helicopter flying in a distance. I cried for help as I quickly reached out for a flare and pop it up but... It flew over me and eventually crashed down into the field not so far away.
I thought I was safe but nowhere is safe... I drove over just to see what's left of the crash site and the infected crew, airborne must have gotten into them and makes their bird lose their control...

I started to question myself If he was still here with me, watching from above as I struggled and thrive to survive... Just a little hope that will make me make it to the next day.

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_72_Content:
What to do in an Emergency
Stay calm! This is the best thing to do! Don't feel bad if you feel sad or mad, just think about it!
Stay inside! Unless there's a flood, we should all stay inside unless we need to get some sun!
Stay occupied! We can play board games, tell stories, dress up in silly costumes, and more!
Stay fasting! Food might be hard to get. So let's only eat a little bit, like we're out camping!
Stay safe! Strangers might come to the house. While some will be nice, we can't help everyone!
Thank God for everything we have - our house, our lives, and most of all our family!

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_7_Content:
A month and week passed... In the evening summer as I was drinking to forget the reality I can't forget about that day on how it take his life forever, away from my life. It got me thinking and pushed myself to find him once again, it was the Riverside church... went back there and it was quiet and beautiful as usual apart from a wall of blood that I painted red.

That day, we fled out of the church and went into one of the houses, he was holding the door but then it broke down before... they mauled him alive, I could only run away and don't look back. Now I am here again in the house where I last saw him, there is a pile of blood, guts, and flesh all around but no sign of him but a trail of blood that leads to the backyard of the house. I followed the trail as what've his remains started to appear more and more and eventually, his hand with still a wedding ring on it... the same one as mine, as I was looking down at it I heard weird knocking sounds behind a woods and hoping to myself that it would be him and when I see it... I can't believe my own eyes.

It was my husband, Jim. With his half, the bottom of his body from his stomach was torn off, both of his hands as well, and one missing eyeball. Still in that black suit like on that wedding day, bloodied and muddied... beyond recognizable but I know it is him.
I- I can't hold myself back from this and not breaks into tears and collapse down, looking at him as he tried to reach out for me to take a bite but he was in a bad shape that he can't even crawl to me.
In the end, I finished him and set him free from this pain... for ever.

I brought what's left of his body back afterward to a proper burial, now his grave won't be empty anymore...
I've found you.

After the burial that night, I even dreamed about him, about the world without the infection where we live happily but it was just a fantasy...

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_88_Content:
THE TRUTH OF THE MATTER
I, Mandy Potemkin, am going to kill all of my coworkers and then myself on 7/8/93. I do not intend to do this out of hatred for them, as they are my friends and have done no wrong but what they have been forced to, as I will now. I am not of unsound mind and do not do this out of something as foolish as momentary passion or as worthless as monetary debt. No, I do this to prove to the world the truth of the matter, that we are all victims of a system and government which do not care for us. Our lives have such little worth to our capitalist and authoritarian rulers that we might as well be mindless drones, marching ever onwards, only consuming, never creating. But I believe by killing myself and my friends, I may not only save us from suffering any longer into this worthless future, but too damage the machinations of our seemingly untouchable overlords and prove to others like us that we can make a difference if only we act and react with haste and with force. This is the truth of the matter, that violence must be done.

I plan to enact my plan first by:

"It ain't nothing personnal, Kriss-X, but as you are the daughter of the Gemstone King, I am sworn to fulfill my destiny and end your empire, freeing the people forever. Lay down the Lightblade and I will make it quick."
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_8_Content:
3 Months later... How long can I keep going? I ask myself this question every dawn and sunset as I am uncertain about the current life I am having. I woke up, I go kill those rotten walking corpses, I live and repeat. It seems like I have no goals in my life but to keep living for him that... Does it still worth it? Do I make him proud of me? Or I should be the one who's up there instead... Maybe I died on the same day as you on our wedding day just so I can see and you stay with me forever. 

I am not sure but I started to hear some voices lately, but it was just me and no one else. Was that your voice calling me when I don't wanna keep going? Was that you that always calm me down when I want to end my own life?
*Am I going insane?*

The feelings of anxiety and loneliness are slowly breaking through the cracks like poison in my bone. Sometimes I am not sure which sounds is real anymore... but his voice always comforts me and it keeps me going, although how can I keep going like this?

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_91_Content: Chris, we are NOT going to JPG! Even if we could get across the bridges (because not all of us can swim, Chris!) into Indiana, do you know how crazy it is to try to get into ANY military base? You should just try walking right into Fort Knox! I get that JPG seemed all nice and peaceful when we went there as kids, but this isn't a field trip, and nobody (not even the soldiers) know where not to step in that place to not get blown into tiny chunks. Hell, the entire range might be freaking radioactive! Listen, dude, we just need to find somewhere quiet to wait this whole thing out, and it doesn't need to be 100 miles away in an old bomb test site, alright? We're over at Michelle's if you want to hang out, but leave this at home, OK? Love you.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_92_Content: A farmer looked over his crops and saw they were wilting for there had been no rain for a week. He went to the hill and asked of the highest powers to bring rain so that those who depended on him would not know hunger. And the rains came and stayed for two weeks, tearing down an immense oak which grew over the farmer's home and smashed it all. He again went to the hill and cursed the rain, demanding for it to stop. And so the rain stopped and returned the sun, endless and blazing, for two months, burning the farmer's crop and stripping the whole land of life. He returned to the hill and with parched lips begged only for shade. And the sunset arrived only for sunrise to never come, leaving the world dark. Unable to see, the farmer could not find the hill again, and so all creation was plunged into lifeless darkness forever.

Liz, a guy came in with a freaky order that I need your help with, also figured you might get a kick out of it. So here this guy is, decked out in full hunting gear, like, y'know, camo everything, fake leaves, face paint that makes him look like a baby barfed on his face, and he asks for all the books and mags we can get on - wait for it - farming. Wants anything about digging in dirt and watering plants going all the way back to 1776. Said he knew everything he needed to about everything else - no sh!t - but couldn't tell a potato from a pumpkin except that one's served with your Spiffo's #1 and the other's in his nana's Thanksgiving pie. What a character, right?

Anyway, I can get all that stuff for him. But then he asked for - and you knew it was coming - every issue of HottieZ going back to 1965. Said anything older makes him feel like he's perving on his mom. I figure your girl in Nashville's gotta have a supply of them, and I bet this guy isn't going to be picky if they're repros or microfiche dupes, so if you can work that angle, be my guest. Man, people are getting weird out there, huh?

See you Monday!
Larry

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_96_Content:
7-8-93
Got back from a run to the farmer's market (almost got into a fight with some roadrager in a Rancher, people are starting to lose it) just to find the door busted open. Some jackass looter broke in and wrecked the place. But that's all it looks like he did, cause as far as I can tell nothing's missing. What the hell? Guess I know what I'm doing for the rest of the evening.

OK. Strike that. The guy did take some stuff, but just my floppies. Pulled every one out of the bins and even the DOS copy out of the drive. Now if I could just figure out why. I guess some people do have weird klepto fetishes, but old disks never would cross my mind. Hope he likes playing GRIM and reading BBS convos from five years ago. Just strange.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_97_Content: I'm not making it down to the Lower Depths, looks like, so I'll just sit here and write. Put it out there into the night air. Conway better be taking care of Lysette, not that I don't expect him to. He's shaped up a lot since he quit the liquor, and she's needed him to since her mind's been going. Hardest thing he's ever done, I'd wager, sobering up just to sit and watch her slip into the dark. Might be a kindness on the part of God, honestly, her forgetting, ever since Charlie and Ira. Might be the wrath of Him that Conway's got to sit and be the only one to remember between the two. Can't ever repay that debt he thinks Lysette's owed. I pity the old guy.\n\nJunebug and Johnny came through a week or so before they put up the border. She seemed to know there was something coming, like she always does, seeing things before and after they've happened. Wish I'd gone with them, though it's not like I'd fit in the sidecar between Johnny, their gear, and that beautiful old dress. They were going to the bar for a gig and we'd all have been there days before the camo guys rolled in. Probably halfway to Santiago by now, riding hard through the nights, gas needle always on zero. Or maybe they're holding out in that old mine they used to hang around. Envy them that, being young and able. Suppose that's my late reflection, hah hah.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_98_Content:
Daryl,
So here's what me and Marty figured out. The army's got all the airfields locked down but they ain't watching any of the dirt strips right? Well we're gonna get the old cropduster out of the barn and roll it down to Sally's to try and see if she'll help us get it flying again. Then we'll all jump in and take off for the Keys. How's that sound huh? It worked in Nam right? And it ain't like they'll scramble to shootdown some little duster flying around. So if you wanna join in we're gonna be starting the roll on Tueday and heading down Old Mill toward Lickskillet. We sure could use your help and I'd get Marty to let you set up front.
Your pal,
Ronnie
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_99_Content: July 7, 1993\nSome f!cker BIT ME today! Like, what the sh!t, dude!? He came stumbling up like he was high or something, and when he was just standing there staring at me, I asked if he was OK, and then he, like, fell over on me and totally BIT ME! Rocky got him off me, and the guy was just flopping around on the sidewalk after that, so maybe he was totally high, but, like, dude!? He bit me so hard, and now I'm all messed up! Hope he liked the taste of f!cking silicone! So Rocky's taking me to the doc tomorrow to get some antibiotics or whatever, make sure it's not infected, and maybe fix the damage. He's so sweet. Maybe I'll pick out a new blouse, too! Tomorrow's going to be great!
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_9_Content: I never thought I'd miss Mondays, but here we are, in the middle of the zombie apocalypse. It's strange how the little things we took for granted become the things we yearn for the most. I miss the sound of the alarm clock, the rush to get ready for work, and even the annoying morning traffic.\n\nThose mundane routines gave our lives a sense of purpose and normalcy. Now, every day feels like a battle for survival. But I hold onto the hope that one day, Mondays will return, and we'll complain about them just like we used to.

UI_trait_BootCampDesc: As always a good military training pays back <LINE> +2 Strength, +2 Fitness, +1 Running, +1 Aiming and +1 Reloading
UI_trait_CombatAnxietyDescDF: Although acclimatised to warfare, you were never able to master your battlefied anxiety. <LINE> Stress gains passively over time, and increases in combat.
UI_trait_ElectronicsSpecialistDescDF: You are highly knowledgeable and experienced in electronics-based infiltration. <LINE> +3 Electrical and +2 Mechanic skills. <LINE> Start with learnt Electronics-related recipes. <LINE> Allows you to hotwire vehicles.

UI_trait_NervesOfSteelDescDF: Years of combat experience has acclimatised you to the chaos of warfare, proving your nerves of steel. <LINE> Stress decreases passively over time.
UI_trait_RunNGunDescDF: You are adept in aiming in CQC environments. <LINE> Your movement has no penalty when aiming.
UI_trait_SurvivalSpecialistDescDF: Extensive combat missions in the wilderness have made you an expert in solo survival, even in the most isolated and remote of conditions. <LINE> +3 Foraging, +3 Farming, +3 Fishing, +3 Trapping skills and +2 Axe skills. <LINE> Start with a tent and campfire kit. <LINE> Start with learnt survival-related recipes.
UI_trait_WarHeroDescDF: Your reputation precedes you. <LINE> In a previous mission you showcased exemplary bravery and gallantry beyond the call of duty, earning you one of the most prestigious medals. <LINE> +2 Aiming, +2 Reloading and +2 Running skills.

UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_I:
FOUND NEAR MULDRAUGH - [date smudged] 
 
I don't know who's gonna read this. Maybe nobody. But someone's gotta write it down before we all forget what's real and what ain't. 
 
It started maybe a week after the blockade. Tommy Culver - you know Tommy, works at the Zippee Mart - he'd been using his granddaddy's hatchet to put down the dead ones. Said he noticed it first around kill thirty or so. The blade felt different. Lighter. Like it WANTED to swing. 
 
We thought he was losing it. Stress'll do that. But then Mary Chen said the same thing about her kitchen knife. And old Harlan with his splitting maul. 
 
The weapons are waking up. 
 
Pastor Mike says it's the souls of the dead, trapped in the metal. Revenge or something. The Wilkins boy - the one who watches all them horror tapes - he says it's like Evil Dead. The blood's doing something. 
 
All I know is this: you kill enough of them with the same tool, something STIRS inside it. We're calling it "The Stir" for now. First stage, the weapon gets a little something extra. Folks been calling these early changes "Marks." 
 
What follows is what we've documented so far. God help us all. 
 
- R.L. Morrison, Muldraugh Survivors Coalition
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_II:
RECOVERED FROM WEST POINT SAFEHOUSE - FIELD NOTES, UNDATED 
 
Continued observations on the phenomenon locally designated "The Stir." 
 
Subject weapons that have accumulated significant termination counts (est. 40-80 confirmed kills) exhibit measurable changes that I cannot explain within any existing framework. 
 
I have performed Rockwell hardness testing on three subject blades. Civilian hatchet ("Tommy's hatchet" per local designation): initial reading 56 HRC, consistent with standard carbon steel. Current reading: 63 HRC. This is metallurgically impossible without rehardening. No heat source was applied. I tested twice. The numbers are correct. 
 
Edge retention on subject blades has increased approximately 340% over baseline. One machete has maintained its factory edge through an estimated 200+ impacts with bone and cartilage. I resharpened my control blade four times in the same period. 
 
Weight measurements are inconsistent. The same axe reads differently on the same scale taken minutes apart. Variance of +/- 0.3kg with no material added or removed. The old coal miner (civilian, name withheld) observed me struggling with this and said: "The hills have always known. You can't weigh something that's waking up." 
 
I am a scientist. I do not have a theory for this. I have measurements that should not exist. 
 
PRACTICAL OBSERVATION: Weapons exhibiting these enhanced properties demonstrate approximately 2-3x the performance gains of initial Marks. Survivors should be encouraged to maintain and develop their affected weapons rather than switching to fresh equipment. The bond appears cumulative and irreversible. 
 
- Dr. Sarah Chen, CDC Field Team 7 
- [Note in different handwriting: "Found her notes. Didn't find her."]
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_III:
JOURNAL FRAGMENT - WATER DAMAGED - DATE UNKNOWN 
 
[Previous pages missing or illegible] 
 
...and that's when I knew it wasn't just in my head. 
 
I set the machete down on the kitchen counter last night. Blade pointing left, same as always. Woke up and it was turned around. Handle toward my hand. Like it was ready for me. 
 
Could've been the wind. Could've been anything. But the balance is different now too. It used to pull to the right - cheap blade, always did. Now it sits perfectly in my grip. I didn't adjust anything. It adjusted to ME. 
 
Old Harlan says his maul is the same way. Says the head feels heavier on the downswing, lighter on the return. "Like it knows which direction the dead ones are," he said. He won't look at it when he's not using it. 
 
The Wilkins boy calls these the "Violent" ones. Says the weapon's changing faster now. Adapting. He showed me his VHS of Hellraiser and said "that's what we're dealing with, man. Blood and pain and something that LIKES it." 
 
He might be crazy but he ain't wrong. 
 
The blade hasn't done anything I'd call scary. Not yet. But when I hold it, I can feel something in the metal. Something patient. Something that wasn't there before. 
 
If you're reading this and you got a weapon that's gone Violent - don't abandon it. Don't let it go. It chose you. For better or worse. 
 
[Remaining pages torn out]
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_IV:
PRIVATE JOURNAL - PASTOR MICHAEL REEVES - ROSEWOOD 
 
The Lord tests us in ways I no longer understand. 
 
I blessed Brother Thompson's crowbar tonight. He asked me to. Said it felt wrong and he wanted God's hand on it. I held it and said the words and I felt... I don't know what I felt. Warmth. Not from the metal - from INSIDE the metal. Like holding a sleeping animal. 
 
I told him it was fine. I told him God's grace covered all things. 
 
I lied. 
 
Sister Martinez's fire axe burns cold to the touch now. COLD. And yet it cleaves through bone like butter left in the sun. She killed nine of the risen dead in a single sweep yesterday. Nine. I counted the bodies. 
 
These weapons they call "Consuming" - they are no longer tools. When Thompson swings that crowbar, the air itself seems to scream. When Martinez holds her axe, her eyes go somewhere else. Somewhere I can't follow. 
 
The Sauced. The Vampiric. The Reaper's blade. 
 
These are not names we gave them. These are names they TOLD us. 
 
I do not know if God has armed us for the final battle or if we have merely traded our souls for survival. What I know is that when I held Thompson's crowbar and said my blessing, something in the metal heard me. 
 
And I am not certain it was God that answered. 
 
(Margin note, later date: "Tommy Culver's hatchet finally talked to him last night. He won't say what it said. He hasn't stopped crying.")
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_V:
HANDWRITTEN ON MOTEL STATIONERY - DIXIE BOY MOTOR LODGE 
 
Okay so nobody believed me about this for like three weeks but I finally got proof. 
 
After a weapon gets its Mark - after the Stir takes hold - there's something ELSE that can happen. Something deeper. We're calling it "The Bond." 
 
You know those old ghost stories where a samurai's sword contains his soul? It's like that but REAL and also way more messed up. 
 
Once you've killed enough with a Marked weapon - and I mean A LOT more, we're talking triple digits easy - the weapon doesn't just wake up more. It bonds to YOU. It becomes part of you somehow. 
 
The Bonds are different from the Marks. Marks change how the weapon fights. Bonds change what the weapon IS. Some get tougher. Like, WAY tougher - the Eternal ones basically don't break anymore. Some get lighter, faster. Some just... refuse to stop. 
 
And here's the creepy part: you can't really give away a Bonded weapon. I mean you CAN, but it feels wrong. Like leaving part of yourself behind. And the new person says it doesn't work as good for them. 
 
We're not just using these weapons anymore. 
 
We're BECOMING them. 
 
- Jamie Wilkins, Age 17 
  Muldraugh Horror Club (membership: 1)
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_VI:
FIELD REPORT - KNOX NATIONAL GUARD OUTPOST ECHO 
 
I'm not writing this for the scientists. The scientists are dead. 
 
I'm writing this because whoever finds this outpost needs to know what their weapons can do. The phenomenon the civilians call "The Stir" - it affects firearms too. If you've been using the same weapon since the outbreak, you already know. If you haven't, start now. 
 
What I've observed in my unit: 
 
Corporal Webb's M16 auto-corrects. Not mechanically - there's no computer in a '92 Colt. But it tracks center mass like it knows where the target is. Webb says he stopped aiming two weeks ago. He just points and the rifle does the rest. 
 
Sergeant Delgado's shotgun cycles faster than the action should physically allow. I've timed it. The mechanism moves quicker than the spring tension should permit. It shouldn't be possible. It is. 
 
My sidearm hasn't jammed in three hundred kills. It's a twenty-year-old Beretta that used to stovepipe every other magazine. Now it runs like it just left the factory. Better than the factory. 
 
I don't care WHY this is happening. I care that it IS. 
 
STANDING ORDERS: Do NOT discard a weapon that's exhibiting. Maintain it. Use it. It will keep you alive longer than any replacement off the rack. What follows is a catalog of observed manifestations in affected firearms. 
 
- Gunnery Sergeant Marcus Cole 
  Kentucky National Guard (Dissolved)
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_VII:
AUDIO TRANSCRIPT - RECOVERED TAPE RECORDER - WEST POINT 
 
[Recording begins mid-sentence] 
 
...don't even need to reload sometimes. I know that sounds insane. I KNOW. But I'm telling you, I've been carrying this Colt since the third day and something's changed. 
 
It holds more rounds now. I counted. Counted twice. Six rounds in a cylinder that only FITS six rounds. Except now it's eight. Then it was ten. I stopped counting after that. 
 
[Sound of distant gunfire] 
 
The gun dreams. I know how that sounds but I'm not - I'm NOT crazy. When I sleep, I can feel it. Dreaming next to me. Hungry. Eager for morning. 
 
Terri's rifle is the same way. Reloads in half the time now. Not because she's faster - because the gun is. Like it's helping. Like it wants to get back in the fight. 
 
[Long pause] 
 
There's a guy came through from Fort Knox. Said before everything went dark, the eggheads were talking about "sympathetic metallurgy." Said the infection might have some kind of... I don't know... some kind of ability to imprint on inorganic matter. Make it part of the hive mind or whatever. 
 
I don't think that's it though. I think it's simpler. I think the guns are just learning. 
 
Learning to kill. 
 
And they're getting REALLY good at it. 
 
[Recording ends] 
 
NOTE: Speaker unidentified. Recorder found in abandoned vehicle on Route 31.
UI_VorpallySauced_CompIntro_VIII:
FINAL ENTRY - CHARRED PAGES - LOCATION UNKNOWN 
 
[Most of the journal is burned. Only fragments remain.] 
 
...finally understood what the old miner meant. "The hills have always known." 
 
My machete stopped wearing down around kill one-fifty. By two hundred, the blade actually started to HEAL. I watched a chip fill itself in overnight. Metal doesn't do that. Metal CAN'T do that. 
 
But it did. 
 
[Several pages missing] 
 
...called it "becoming Blooded." Said his granddaddy's hunting rifle did the same thing back in '18. During the Spanish flu. Said weapons that drink enough death eventually refuse to die themselves. 
 
I thought he was crazy. Now I understand. 
 
The weapon doesn't just bond to you at that point. It becomes you. Your heartbeat syncs with its weight. Your dreams are its dreams. When you swing it, you don't think about swinging anymore than you think about breathing. 
 
[Burn marks obscure several lines] 
 
...Tommy Culver finally stopped crying. His hatchet talked to him, he said. Told him its name. He won't share what it said, but he's different now. Calmer. Steadier. He holds the hatchet everywhere he goes now. Sleeps with it. 
 
The other day someone asked if they could borrow it. Tommy just smiled and said no. Not angry. Not scared. Just... sure. 
 
That scares me more than anything. 
 
[Final readable section] 
 
If you're reading this and you've got a weapon that's gone Blooded - congratulations. You've done something impossible. You've killed enough of them that the boundary between you and your weapon has dissolved. 
 
You're not a survivor anymore. 
 
You're something else entirely. 
 
- R.L. Morrison, Muldraugh 
  [Date burned away]

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_ofBloodth: There's a hunger to it now. I can feel it when I swing. The damage is real but the want is realer.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_ofRebirth: It shouldn't still be in one piece. It is. I've stopped questioning it and started being grateful.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_ofTransce: Every axis improved. Not a lot on each one. But all of them. All at once. Weapon's become something it wasn't. I have too.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_ofWhisper: It takes more of them in one swing than it has any right to. I heard something in my head the first time it happened. Not words. Just a feeling. Satisfied.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_oftheCons: When it crits it really crits. And it crits a lot. I don't know what it consumed to get here. I don't think I want to know.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_oftheCove: It hits harder and it finds the vital spot more often. Like we made an agreement. Like something was agreed to that I wasn't part of, and I've benefited anyway.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_oftheUndy: The condition doesn't move. The max doesn't lower. It gets hit and it holds. I don't know what it learned from the blood, but it learned something.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Bonding_oftheWiel: It moves with me now. Fast and mean and exactly where I need it. The pushback is wrong — too strong. But the speed is wronger.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FBonding_ofTrueAi: It aims itself. That's not an exaggeration. The barrel finds the line before I've finished the thought. And then it fires faster than I can plan.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FBonding_oftheArs: More in the mag than there used to be and empty again faster than seems possible. Speed and volume together. It never runs dry at the wrong moment.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FBonding_oftheGun: Fifty percent faster reload and fires so fast between shots I stopped thinking of them as separate. This gun belongs to a different kind of fight.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FBonding_oftheMar: On target before I'm ready. Critting more than I should. This gun has a sense of occasion.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FBonding_oftheOpe: Hits harder, aims truer, gets on target faster. It's committed to the job in a way that goes beyond the metal it's made from.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FBonding_oftheVet: Accurate. Reliable. Durable. Reloads fast. It's like it's been through all of this before and decided to get better at it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Annihilat: I don't aim for center mass anymore. The shot handles that part.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Brutal: Bodies are stopping faster. I don't know what that means for the gun. I know what it means for me.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Bullseye: I aimed it once today. Once. The rest was just reflex. All of them landed.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Combat: The delay between shots is almost nothing. The gun is angrier than I am.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Cyclic: It's barely pausing between rounds. My finger feels like it's not even part of the process.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Deadeye: Long shots. More crits. I'm watching them from farther away and putting them down cleaner. The gun made a deal with physics and didn't tell me.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Deadly: Running shot, panicking, low light — still connected. Something in the gun wants to connect.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Devastati: One burst today. One. I had to check that they were really down.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Execution: I stopped compensating for drift. The gun compensates.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Extended: I don't know how far that last shot went. Far enough. That's what matters.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_FullAuto: I lost track of the individual shots. There was just a sound and then silence.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Gunfighte: By the time they see me, I've already shot twice. The draw, the aim, the crit — it's all collapsed into one motion.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Honed: Something changed in the barrel, maybe. Or in me. The hits are heavier now.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Keen: The timing is better. The ones I shouldn't hit, I sometimes hit. More often now.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Long: Connected at a range that surprised me. Surprised them too, probably.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Marksmans: Every shot counts for more now. The accuracy, the crits, the time it takes to get there — all of it moving in the right direction.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Merciless: It puts the round where it needs to go. Every time. I'm mostly just holding it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Operators: Accurate, fast, and it hurts when it hits. I don't know what I did to earn this.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Precise: Shots are landing where I point it. Actually landing. That wasn't always the case.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_QuickFire: The next shot is ready a little sooner than I expect. Small thing. Adds up.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Rapid: I'm shooting faster than I'm aiming. It doesn't seem to matter.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Reaching: I held the corner and still put shots downrange. More downrange than I should have.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Responsiv: It cycles back like it's in a hurry. I can keep the pace now.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Sauced: Critical hits I shouldn't have made, accuracy I didn't earn, damage that ends arguments. It's too much in all the right ways.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Savage: It's putting things down in fewer rounds. I'd call that a gift.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Sharp: Every shot punches deeper than it should. I checked the ammo. Same ammo.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Sighted: Whatever I point it at, it finds. Not every time. But closer to every time than before.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Snipers: The shot goes where my eyes say to send it. Not approximately. Exactly.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Steady: The barrel settles faster. The wobble is almost gone.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Tactical: Faster and more likely to connect. The rate of fire and the accuracy together — the gun is doing math I can't do.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_TrueAim: Stopped missing the second shot. That used to always drift.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Vicious: It found the gap twice today. The angle I needed and couldn't have made on my own.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Warzone: High damage and I can shoot fast and I can hit things far away. This is not a fair fight. I am grateful for that.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FPrefix_Zeroed: It's locked. I don't know how to describe it better than that. Locked on.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofAbundan: I shoot more and reload less. The math of it doesn't add up. I've checked.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofCapacit: A few more rounds before I'm fishing for a mag. Enough to make a difference.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofDestruc: I've stopped thinking of it as a per-shot calculation. It's more of a verdict.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofEnduran: This thing was not built to stop working. I've tested that.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofEternit: I don't know what to clean anymore. The wear just doesn't come.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofExecuti: I had a shot today I'll remember for a while. I won't describe it. I'll just remember it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofFocus: The sight picture settles just a little faster. Small window. Worth having.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofFortitu: Three months. No jams from condition. Barely any wear I can see.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofHarm: Rounds are hitting a little harder. Same ammo. The gun does something to them.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofInfinit: I kept shooting and shooting and the mag kept going. I was almost embarrassed when it finally ran dry.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofInstinc: I'm on target before my brain finishes the command. The gap is closing.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofLethali: When it crits, the conversation ends. Immediately.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofLoading: I'm back in the fight before I expect to be. Good surprise.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofMastery: I cleaned it today out of habit. It didn't need it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofPermane: I've stopped worrying about it breaking down. That used to take up a lot of space in my head.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofPrecisi: The crits sting more than they should. Something in the timing amplifies it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofPreserv: Takes longer to wear out. Not forever. Just longer. That's enough.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofQuality: The degradation is slower. I'd say half as fast. Maybe better.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofQuietin: The report was softer. Not silent, but the block didn't turn. Fewer came.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofReliabi: Jammed once in the last month. Once. I almost didn't believe it when it happened.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofReloadi: Slightly faster getting the mag in. I feel it in the rhythm.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofResilie: Took it through conditions I wouldn't take my boots through. Still running.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofSilence: I fired from the roof. The horde below kept walking. Like I wasn't there.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofSpeed: The reload is almost automatic now. I don't think about it. I just do it and I'm done.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofStorage: Ran through a horde without reloading. Didn't used to be able to do that.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofSuppres: The shot left my hands and the sound stayed behind. The dead don't know I'm here.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofSwiftne: Hands do the job before I've finished the thought. I've had it for weeks and I'm still surprised.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofTrueFun: It feeds. Every time. I've stopped flinching when I pull the trigger.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_ofWoundin: They go down in fewer shots. That's the whole thing. Fewer shots.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheArmo: More capacity, faster reload, hits harder. It's not one improvement. It's all of them, pointing in the same direction.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheArse: I've started treating it like it's inexhaustible. That's an attitude you earn, not assume.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheAssa: Aim fast, crit hard, hit heavy. Everything collapses into a single terrible moment.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheComm: Reloads fast. Holds more. Doesn't wear down like it should. It's like it's trying to keep me alive.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheFait: I put a round in the chamber and I know it will fire. That's not a small thing. That's not a small thing at all.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheGuns: I reloaded mid-horde and nobody got me. That's not nothing.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheImmo: It refuses to fail. Stubbornly, consistently, in defiance of everything. Refuses.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheMaga: The mag holds more than the numbers on the side say. I counted. It holds more.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheProf: It stays in good shape, aims quicker, and degrades like it's refusing to. This gun has professional standards.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheQuic: Empty to loaded to shooting so fast I thought I'd miscounted the mag. I hadn't. It was just that quick.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheRefl: I snap it up and it's already where I need it. Muscle memory except I didn't build this memory.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheSauc: Durable and then more durable. I've stopped being surprised when it keeps working.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheSold: Reload time almost nothing. Condition barely budges. Extra rounds in the mag. This is a weapon that was made for exactly this.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_FSuffix_oftheVete: Aims fast, reloads fast, and when it crits it really means it. Competence in one package.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Annihilati: I stopped counting what comes back out when I pull it away. Easier that way.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Executione: It wants the skull. Every swing wants the skull. I've stopped arguing with it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Extended: The nearest one is never where my eyes said it was. I keep hitting them anyway.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Honed: The resistance is gone. It goes through like they're not even trying to stop it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Immolating: The last one caught fire. The one before it too. I don't think it's me doing that.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Inexhausti: I swung until I wanted to stop, not until I had to. That's new.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Keen: Something changed. I'm landing hits I shouldn't be, on the first try.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Lightning: My arm can barely keep up with it. My shoulder aches in a new way.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Long: Caught one at a distance that felt too far. Didn't miss.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Merciless: It doesn't miss the killing blow. I'm not sure it's me doing it anymore.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Phantom: It's everywhere before I've moved. The range and speed together make it feel like cheating.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Precise: Stopped hesitating after it. The swing finds the spot I mean it to.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Quick: The return is automatic now. I'm not controlling it, just riding it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Rapid: Three of them in the time it used to take for two. I counted.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Prefix_Reaching: I'm keeping more space than I used to and still making contact. Somehow.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofCarnage: The arc keeps taking what's in front of it. I've mostly stopped trying to aim.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofCelerity: The swing comes back and I'm already swinging again. My arms figured it out before my head did.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofEntry: Took a door in two hits. Felt wrong how easy that was.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofEternity: It should be dust by now. The math doesn't work.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofExecutio: I had a crit today that made me take a step back and look at the weapon. Just look at it.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofFortitud: Used it hard for a week. Still looks like I found it yesterday.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofHaste: Slightly quicker than before. Just enough to change the rhythm.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofHushing: The shot was quieter. Not silent, but the echo died fast. The dead didn't come.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofIronWill: I kept swinging past the point I should have had to stop. The weapon carries some of the weight. I swear it does.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_ofPrecisio: When it crits, it really crits. The difference is significant. I felt it immediately.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_oftheEarth: I hit one and it knocked the next one sideways. Couldn't have planned it.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_Suffix_oftheGhost: Fast and slippery and finding the gaps I didn't know were there. It feels like fighting from somewhere they can't quite see.

UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_oftheConsumed: It took something from them. I saw the edge change.
UI_VorpallySauced_Lore_oftheCovenant: Every wound it deals, it keeps

UI_VorpallySauced_MoodNotify_Agitated2: An uneasy tremor in the grip.
UI_VorpallySauced_MoodNotify_Calm2: A quiet settles over the weapon.

UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Anxious_Desc: It feels your fear, and hates it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Cold_Desc: Just a tool. Nothing has marked it.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Damp_Desc: Rain and red run together. Nothing sticks.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Dreaming_Desc: Late and still. It dreams of edges it has met.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Dripping_Desc: It won't come clean. It doesn't try.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Drowsing_Desc: Idle and indoors. It dozes against your side.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Feral_Desc: Blooded in the dark. It pulls toward the next one.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Flickering_Desc: Your dread strikes a spark in it, then nothing.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Gloaming_Desc: The light goes. It feels the long dark coming on.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Gorged_Desc: Slick to the grip and full — and hungry anyway.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Greying_Desc: Grey at the edges — you've lasted the night. It eases.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Humming_Desc: Quiet warmth in the daylight. Content, briefly.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Hunting_Desc: Half-fed in the dark, casting for more.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Quiet_Desc: No voice in it — only the weight of the dead.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Remembering_Desc: Quiet — but it counts the dead it has made.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Restless_Desc: It won't settle. It paces in your hand.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Rinsing_Desc: The rain takes the blood. It lets go, for now.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Roused_Desc: Awake to the work now. It wants the rhythm to hold.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Settling_Desc: Clean and sheltered, it forgets what it saw.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Singing_Desc: It rings between every blow. It does not want to stop.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Still_Desc: Resting. Patient. It has all the time there is.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Straining_Desc: Heavier than it was. It blames your tired arm.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Thirsting_Desc: Clean under a dead sky. It wants that to change.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Trembling_Desc: Too much death, too fast — it shudders to keep up.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Uneasy_Desc: The dark leans in. It almost understands why.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Warm_Desc: The blood leaves a warmth it can't name.
UI_VorpallySauced_Mood_Watchful_Desc: Awake in the dark, listening with you.

UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_AnyAdvice:
When you enter the arena, remember you are part of the installation. Perform with vigor.

The more spectacular your... decommissioning of the other exhibits... the more valuable the echoes you'll yield for my collection.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_CanWeBargain:
Haggle? With me?

My good fellow, I have acquired treasures from ruins history itself has forgotten.

My price is the final word.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_Default:
I am the Curator.

You are standing inside my masterpiece.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_TheUndead:
Marvelous, aren't they?

The zombies provide such a wonderful sense of physicality.

The ghosts, on the other hand, offer a more... ethereal aesthetic.

A balanced collection needs both.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_TryHonestyWager:
Ah. You're the one he sent. Of course you are. Try Honesty never comes himself when pride might be spared by distance.

Yes, I kept the Brass Bout Bell. He lost it fairly, however loudly he may remember otherwise. A fountain was used, the terms were broken, and the bout ceased to be a bout at all.

He believes a cheering crowd can correct a ruined condition. He is wrong. Frequently, and with style.

Still, I am told you performed well. Better than most of the meat he throws into that pit. That gives me hope.

So take the bell. Not as settlement of his grievance, but as an investment in yours.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_TryHonestyWagerCla:
The Brass Bout Bell is yours now.

Take it back to Try Honesty. I am certain he will mistake retrieval for vindication.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_WhatDoYouSell:
I provide the tools for the exhibits to... refine themselves.

I accept the resonant echoes left behind by the... decommissioned performers... and in return, I lend out superior artifacts to those who show promise.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_WhatIsThisPlace:
You are in the Carrion Ascension.

The centerpiece of my exhibition on mortal transience and posthumous endeavor.

The fights below are a... dynamic sculpture. A study in conflict.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
I am the Curator.

This crypt, this arena, the very echoes that cling to the air... all of it is part of my permanent collection.

You are standing inside my masterpiece.
UI_CHCynthiaElias_Bubble_Entry01:
Cynthia: Someone's here, Elias. Do you feel it? They feel... real.
Elias: I know... The whole place felt it, sister.
Cynthia: Do you think they've come for us?
Elias: If they have, the Warden will find them first.
UI_CHCynthiaElias_Bubble_Entry02:
Cynthia: They're inside. Elias... they really went in. Why would it let them in?
Elias: It shouldn't have... Maybe it wants something from them.
Cynthia: That's what worries me.
UI_CHCynthiaElias_Bubble_Entry03:
Cynthia: They're really going down there?
Elias: Hm. Seems so.
Cynthia: The Warden must think highly of them... if he's letting them near Father's arena.
Elias: I don't think that's why he let them through.
Cynthia: Then we'll see what he wants with them.

UI_CHLyra_Bubble_Intro:
Careful with the cards you clutch so tightly. Some of their threads run deeper than this crypt, down past the bedrock, into a place the church stopped naming.

She listens there. She likes curious hands.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_CallasFamily:
In the records, the Callas look immaculate: the family appointed to stand between the church and the place below, after the first archivist - the one they bound down there - the one that had to be contained.

The wards beneath don't listen to prayers. They listen to blood. Callas blood opens doors other people can only die in front of.

So the church called it duty. Privilege. Legacy.

She reads it differently. To her, the Callas line has always been a promise: that where the margins of her own bloodline bled into theirs, a Callas girl would be born more key than child - ink and Callas blood braided into a vessel made to fit the one below.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_Default:
Careful with the cards you clutch so tightly. Some of their threads run deeper than this crypt, down past the bedrock, into a place the church stopped naming.

She listens there. She likes curious hands.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_UndyingOnes:
You call them undying.

I see bodies whose stories were cut wrong and stitched back by a will that refuses endings.

Some of what's wrong here is older than that. Those people died the way people are meant to.

Flesh to soil, breath to silence. It's their souls that never made it out - thin, stubborn echoes pinned here, because this estate and the place below drink from the same poisoned vein.

The others are different. They went down into the place below and left too much of themselves within her reach.

What crawled back up wears their meat, but there isn't a story inside anymore... just hunger, hanging off a borrowed thread.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_UnspoiledGraceAccepte:
Then we ask water to remember what it was before it learned to bargain.

Find the vial Marlowe kept. Untouched grace can rinse noise from a vision without teaching it to bite back.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_UnspoiledGraceTurnedI:
There. The thread finds its pattern again.

The static recedes, and the image of the Sanctum begins to gather back into shape. You did well.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhatAreTheseCards:
On the surface?

Just pictures, numbers, promises. Underneath, they're pages torn from lives that already happened - memories that slipped the binding.

Each card is an echo of a story you never got to live. When you hand me a set, I press that story into one shape and give it a body again.

You call it an item.
I call it... closure.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhereFindCards:
Anywhere the place below brushes against the surface.

They cling to things that kept moving after their story should have stopped, and to those who walked too far into the wrong corridors and didn't come back whole.

If a road feels like it's straying toward the depths, watch what falls there.

The cards are drawn to that kind of ruin.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
Who am I...?

That depends which one of you is asking.

Up here they write it as Lyra, Weaver of Threads. Sounds tidy, doesn't it?

As if any of this was done on purpose.

I listen to the loose strands that got caught in your cards - the bits of you that almost were, or were once already.

I give them something solid to become, and you walk away thinking it was just a trade.

As for who I was before...

She remembers better than I do.

The one below.

I try not to use her name; it has a habit of answering back.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhoIsShe:
She was the one who filed other people's truths into neat little rows. An archivist, breathing dust and ink, lingering in the forbidden margins no one was meant to read.

Then the words stopped lying still for her. They slipped off the page, wound themselves around her thoughts... and a few important stitches came loose.

The church called it heresy. The place below called it an opening.

Now she's more pull than person - a will moving along the deeper threads, looking for a loose one like yours to tug.

I don't use her name. Names are doorhandles, and she's very good at turning them.
UI_CHLyra_DivinationUnavailableSay: Lyra's transmutation is not available right now.
UI_CHMarlowe_DialogueOption_WhatDeals: What kind of deals does it offer?
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_AreYouControllingI:
Controlling it? Good heavens, no.

I simply understand its manners better than most.
My dear friend, everyone uses something. Tools, faith, fear, other people. I am merely more polite about it.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_ChooseYourFateAcce:
Excellent. The fountain is waiting, and it adores decisive customers.

Take one bargain. Any one. Return when the water has marked the transaction, and I will release the vial.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_ChooseYourFateTurn:
There we are. Paid in consequence, sealed by the fountain, witnessed by a man of impeccable bookkeeping.

Take the vial to Lyra. And do try to remember who kept it safe all these years.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_Default:
Ah, a customer. Or a pilgrim. Hard to tell these days.

Either way, welcome.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting1: Back again? Wonderful. I was beginning to worry you had developed caution.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting2: Come to bargain, or merely to stare at the consequences?
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting3: Careful near the water. It has a talent for overhearing desire.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting4: Ah. My favorite kind of visitor. Alive, curious, and not yet sufficiently warned.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatDeals:
Useful ones. Dangerous ones. The sort people swear they would never accept, until they need them badly enough.

Strength for frailty. Fortune for hunger. Clarity for something you may miss only after it is gone.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatDeals_Response: Most bargains do, when described honestly.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatIsFountain:
Once? A holy little thing, I am told. Graceful, generous, terribly inefficient.

Now? It has matured.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatIsFountain_Res: A blessing for a consequence. That is how the fountain speaks now.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhoAreYou: <accent>Marlowe Veyne</accent>. Collector of rare opportunities, negotiator of regrettable wishes, and, on better days, a perfectly respectable gentleman.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhoAreYou_Response: Charlatan is such an ugly word. I prefer... <accent>specialist in selective truths</accent>.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhyOutHere:
Because this is where people come when prayer has failed, coin has failed, and good sense has failed most of all.

And because the fountain and I have an understanding.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhyOutHere_Respons: I bring it the desperate. It reminds them that nothing worth having arrives cleanly.
UI_CHMarlowe_PlayerResponse_Charlatan: That sounds like a lot of words for charlatan.
UI_CHMelora_Bubble_Intro:
Cynthia, if Mr. Klaus sees you out late again... oh.

You're someone else. Forgive me.

The water keeps returning the wrong reflections.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_Default:
Cynthia, if Mr. Klaus sees you out late again... oh.

You're someone else. Forgive me.

The water keeps returning the wrong reflections.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_DoYouNeedHelp:
No... no, I'm fine.

I have everything I need.

But... if you do see Julian, tell him I'll be waiting.

Just a little longer.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_NeverMind:
Of course.

The water's better company, anyway.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
The name is Melora.

I work the kitchens.

Sometimes I help with the little ones when the mistress isn't looking.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_WhyOutHere:
Oh, I like it here.

It's quiet.

The water listens better than people do.
UI_CHMothersCrypt_FoundSomethingInCoffin: I found something in the coffin!
UI_CHQuestLog_a_bell_in_the_ruins_DescRi:
You woke with the sound of a bell in your head.
In the dream, you saw a ruined church beneath a dead sky. Its doors stood open.
Below the floorboards, candlelight flickered.
You do not know why it matters.
But a church may still mean shelter, supplies, or answers.
UI_CHQuestLog_choose_your_fate_DescRich: Marlowe has the Vial of Unspoiled Grace, and no intention of releasing it for something as cheap as gratitude. He calls the fountain honest: one blessing, one consequence, every miracle properly accounted for. Accept one bargain from the fountain, then return to Marlowe and collect the vial.
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_relic_altar_DescR:
Serevine returns the Sanctified Bell to you,
not as a trophy, but with a purpose.
She believes the altar in the chamber beside her was made to receive relics such as this, allowing their sacred influence to endure while bound within it.
Place the Sanctified Bell into the relic altar, then return to Serevine.
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_relic_altar_Objec: Place the <accent>Sanctified Bell</accent> into the <accent>relic altar</accent>
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_the_bell_below_De:
Serevine believes the bell seen in your dream may be the Sanctified Bell, a sacred Valerian relic once sealed somewhere beneath Cedar Hill Church. If she is right, then your dream was no mere imagining.
Descend deeper into the church cellars, uncover the hidden reliquary, recover the Sanctified Bell, and return it to Serevine.
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_the_callas_record:
Serevine has exhausted the church's surviving records of the Sanctuary. They confirm that it once existed, but reveal nothing of its location, its purpose, or the reason it was hidden. The Callas family may have preserved what the church concealed.
Travel to Callas Manor and uncover any record they left behind concerning the Sanctuary.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_ashen_wards_DescRich:
Silas has heard the dead of House Callas stirring within their family cemetery. The wards etched upon their stone coffins are failing, leaving their rest exposed to whatever stirs below.
Take the warding kit, repair the broken wards, and return to Silas once the graves have fallen silent.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_the_invitation_DescR:
Silas believes you have earned an introduction. With the Regal Hatch Key in hand, the way to the Carrion Ascension now lies open.
Beneath the opposite crypt waits an arena few living souls are invited to see.
Descend through the hatch and present your invitation to Try Honesty.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_unquiet_crypt_DescRi: Silas has entrusted you with a grim task. The Mother's Crypt is poisoned by a sorrow that has festered into rage, unsettling the peace of the graveyard. He has given you the key, and charged you to enter the crypt, find the source of the turmoil, and put it to rest by any means necessary.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_warden_call_DescRich:
You heard a voice near the Callas Family Cemetery...

"Ah, a living soul... a rare and welcome sight these days. If you have a moment for an old warden, come, let us speak."

Find the source of the voice among the graves, and learn what stirs there.
UI_CHQuestLog_the_servants_way_DescRich:
Explore the Estate. While the right path leads to the old graveyard, the left fork remains largely unexplored.
It winds past the estate's overgrown greenhouse and down toward the waterline. Perhaps the servants who once walked this route knew secrets their masters had long since forgotten.
UI_CHQuestLog_tryhonesty_crowd_wants_mor:
Try Honesty is not done with you yet.
The crowd has seen you survive. Now they want to know whether you can win without leaning on the fountain like a wounded noble at a garden party.
Complete one full arena match without using the fountain, then return to Try Honesty.
UI_CHQuestLog_tryhonesty_first_match_Des:
Try Honesty has accepted your invitation,
though not without making a spectacle of it.
The Carrion Ascension does not hand out glory freely. Step into the arena, survive one full match, and return to Try Honesty with your dignity mostly intact.
UI_CHQuestLog_tryhonesty_gentlemans_wage:
Try Honesty has decided your survival may yet be useful. An old wager with the Curator ended poorly after a match was soured by technicalities, excuses, and one very inconvenient fountain.
Ask the Curator about the wager, recover the Brass Bout Bell, and return it to Try Honesty.
UI_CHQuestSay_silas_unquiet_crypt_comple: The spirits... they're finally at peace.
UI_CHQuestSay_silas_warden_call_complete: The old warden... what tales he must hold.
UI_CHQuestSay_tryhonesty_crowd_wants_mor: The fountain broke the challenge. I will have to try again.
UI_CHQuestSay_tryhonesty_first_match_com: I made it through the arena.
UI_CHQuestSay_tryhonesty_gentlemans_wage: The bell is back where it belongs.

UI_CHSerevine_Bubble_Church01:
Stop right there. Not a step closer!
...Oh. A person. And alive?
Wonderful. Alarming, but wonderful.
Come in, then. A fellow explorer, I hope.
UI_CHSerevine_Bubble_Church02:
Sorry. You startled me half to death, which is very rude in a place already full of death.
I'm Serevine, Valerian scholar, temporary cellar resident, and currently very grateful you are not trying to eat me.
UI_CHSerevine_Bubble_Church03: Oh, it worked! There is something different about you now. A steadiness, perhaps... as though the Bell has finally found its proper bearer. Leave it upon the altar, and I believe its blessing will remain with you.
UI_CHSerevine_DialogueOption_CallasMap: Is that a map of Callas Manor?
UI_CHSerevine_DialogueOption_DeadWalk: Any idea why the dead walk?
UI_CHSerevine_DialogueOption_DreamChurch: I saw this church in a dream
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_CallasMap:
It is. Remarkable, isn't it?

Every wing, every garden path, even the servants' passages have been recorded in extraordinary detail.

I had expected a parish sketch. This is something far more deliberate.

Though it has one rather curious omission.

The records place Valerian's first sanctuary somewhere beneath the estate.

Yet this map makes no mention of it at all.

For a place of such importance to be absent from a map this precise... I find it very difficult to believe that was an oversight.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_DeadWalk:
Nothing I could honestly call an answer.

But I have found records of visits to a Valerian sanctuary on the Callas estate. Supposedly, the first sanctuary ever raised in His name.

If that is true, it is extraordinary. Thousands of years of history, doctrine, relics... perhaps even accounts from the founding of the faith itself.

I confess, I was rather thrilled when I first understood what I was reading.

Then I reached the later entries. The visits become fewer. People return from the sanctuary described as distant... vacant... diminished.

One account says a man came back breathing, walking, and speaking... yet his wife insisted that whatever returned from beneath the estate was no longer her husband.

I would very much like to dismiss it as frightened superstition. Given what is wandering outside, that has become rather difficult.

If there is an answer beneath the Callas estate, I think we ought to find it.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_DreamChurch:
This church? Before you had ever set foot inside it?
How extraordinary.

Forgive me. I imagine it was rather less extraordinary to experience.

Dreams of sacred sites do appear in old Valerian studies, though never in any account I considered reliable.

There is one detail those accounts repeat with peculiar consistency.

Tell me, did you hear a bell?
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_HeardItRinging:
You did?
Then I may owe several long-dead scholars a sincere apology.

I had always assumed they were describing a symbol, not an actual phenomenon.

Judging by the state of the steeples, I sincerely doubt the tower bell has rung for a very long time.

Yet the accounts describe a bell heard in sleep, calling the living toward sacred ground.

I thought it devotional allegory.

Now you are standing here, in the very church those accounts describe. Which makes this considerably more important than I had hoped.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_RelicAltarAccepte:
Take it. Not as a trophy, but with a purpose.

The altar in the nearby chamber was made to receive relics such as this. If the bell is placed there, its influence may endure without being carried in your hands.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_RelicAltarTurnedI:
Then it worked. There is something steadier in the air now, as though the Bell has finally found its proper bearer.

Leave it upon the altar, and I believe its blessing will remain with you.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheBellBelowAccep:
Then we should treat your dream as evidence, however inconvenient that may be.

The accounts speak of a bell beneath holy ground. If the relic is here, it will not have been left in any ordinary chamber.

Descend below the church. Find what the Valerians sealed away, and bring the bell to me before you bind it to anything.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheBellBelowTurne:
You found it. Valerian's Bell... and not merely a story after all.

There is a sanctified mark beneath the tarnish. Give me a moment with it. If the old rite still answers, I can return it to you as something more than salvage.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheCallasRecordAc:
The church records have taken us as far as they can.

If the Callas family concealed what the Church could not admit, their manor may still hold the missing account. Recover any record they left behind concerning the Sanctuary.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheCallasRecordTu:
This is exactly what I feared, and exactly what I needed.

The Callas record gives shape to the omission. Whatever lies beneath that estate was not forgotten. It was deliberately hidden.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_WhatIsThisPlace:
I had hoped it was only a hidden archive. The scrolls, the sealed records, the fireplace kept for long nights of study... those I can understand.

Though judging by the dust, no one has studied here in centuries.

The cages in the corridor are rather harder to explain. Rust, brittle leather, dust thick enough to bury a confession.

Whatever happened here, it happened long before the dead began walking.

There are restraints here. Instruments meant for questioning, if one wishes to be charitable.

Whatever was recorded in this room, I do not think it was always offered willingly.

That is the part I find most troubling. The restraints bear Valerian seals. The records beside them carry the same insignia.

Whoever used this place was not hiding from the Church. They were acting in its name.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
I study Valerian relics, sacred sites, and the history people usually find more comfortable leaving buried.

I came to Cedar Hill after hearing the rather extraordinary accounts surrounding Callas Manor.

My superiors thought the matter warranted investigation.

Truthfully, I would have come whether they asked or not.

UI_CHSilasAshenWards_AllCorrected: That should be all of them. Silas should know.

UI_CHSilasAshenWards_CleanLine2: The ward holds here. Leave this grave be.
UI_CHSilasAshenWards_CleanLine3: No corruption here. This seal is already correct.
