UI_CHSilasAshenWards_CorruptedLine2: This ward is inverted. Correct this grave seal.
UI_CHSilasAshenWards_CorruptedLine3: The seal is broken here. This grave needs correction.
UI_CHSilasAshenWards_ExamineFirst: I should examine the seal first.
UI_CHSilasAshenWards_NeedSealKit: I need Silas' seal kit for this.
UI_CHSilasAshenWards_RemainingUnstable: The seal settles. {count} still feel unstable.
UI_CHSilas_Bubble_Intro: Greetings, traveler. I am <accent>Silas</accent>, the warden of this place. It is not often I receive visitors who still draw breath.
UI_CHSilas_Bubble_WardenCall: Ah, a living soul... a rare and welcome sight these days. If you have a moment for an old warden, come, let us speak.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_AshenWardsAccepted:
Take the kit. Its tools are modest, but they remember the shape of the old wards.

Examine the grave seals throughout the cemetery. If one answers wrong, correct it before the unrest spreads.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_AshenWardsTurnedIn:
Yes... I can feel it. The stones are quieter now.

You have given the dead a kindness, and the living a little more time.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_CanIHelp:
Perhaps. The wards around this cemetery have begun to fray in ways they should not.

If you are willing, I would ask you to inspect the grave seals, correct what has been miswritten, and return before the unrest deepens.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_Default: Greetings, traveler. I am <accent>Silas</accent>, the warden of this place. It is not often I receive visitors who still draw breath.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_InvitationAccepted:
Then the way is open. Take this invitation.

The place across the grounds will not welcome the living easily, but it should recognize the warden's seal.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_UnquietCryptAccepted:
I see you have taken an interest in the plight of this place. Thank you.

The Mother's Crypt holds a sorrow that has festered into rage.

It disturbs the peace of this entire ground.

Take this key. Enter, and pacify the source of the turmoil.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_UnquietCryptTurnedIn:
The crypt is still at last.

Whatever pain was bound below has loosened its grip. Rest may return to this ground.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
My name is Silas.

I am the keeper of this graveyard, a warden of memories and a tender of final rest.

I have watched over these stones for longer than I care to recall, ensuring the peace of those who reside here.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_WhyOutHere:
This is my purpose.

The living have their bustling cities, and the departed... have this.

Someone must ensure their slumber is not disturbed by the... restless energies that cling to Callas Manor.

It is a quiet duty, but a necessary one.

UI_CHTryHonestyArena_ForfeitSay: You forfeit the arena and leave the pit.

UI_CHTryHonestyArena_RankIncreasedSay: Your arena rank has increased to {rank}.

UI_CHTryHonesty_Bubble_Intro: How delightful. Silas has sent me another mortal who thinks they're meant for more. Give me the invitation. We'll see what survives.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_ArenaRank: Your arena rank is shown below.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_DoYouEnjoyThis:
Enjoy? That's the word mortals use when someone finally does what they were made for.

I don't enjoy it. I am it.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_GentlemansWager:
You've got potential. A rare inconvenience. Most who enter my arena die too quickly to be of use to me.

The Curator and I once placed a gentleman's wager. A relic against the outcome of a bout. Then the match soured, a fountain was touched, and that shrivelled little priest of order decided the rules had been violated.

I say a fighter still breathing is a fighter still in the contest. He says otherwise. Naturally, he wrote the conclusion down and called it truth.

So he kept my stake. The Brass Bout Bell. Without it, the pit is mere spectacle. With it, the bout is sanctioned.

Go to him. Tell him I want the bell returned.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
Name's Try Honesty.

I build the trials that prove what you are and bury what you pretend to be.

UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_Inventory_Desc: Follows the actual position of the player inventory and containers, including panels moved by the player. A single click on another container changes the displayed loot without closing the panels; double-click outside them to close unpinned inventories. OFF restores vanilla behavior.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_Left_Desc: Hides the left sidebar and reveals it only when the cursor enters the panel's real area. While hidden, the vanilla health heart remains visible only during its damage animation. OFF restores vanilla behavior.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_LootProximityKey_Desc: Assign a key to enable or disable automatic nearby-container reveal during gameplay.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_LootProximity_Desc: Reveals the world inventory when the selected nearby container changes. Disable it to keep the panel hidden until you interact with it.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_Minimap_Desc: Fades the open minimap smoothly in its own current area and waits 3.5 seconds after the cursor leaves before fading out. OFF restores vanilla behavior.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_MoodleAlerts_Desc: When a new Moodle appears, brings the right-side group into view with three Morse-like pulses over about five seconds, without changing its color.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_Right_Desc: Moves active Moodles out through the right edge and reveals them from their real occupied area. OFF restores vanilla behavior.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_Speed_Desc: When enabled, the game speed panel is hidden and you control time only with the keyboard shortcuts. When disabled, the panel is visible on the HUD as usual.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_TechnicalInfo_Desc: Shows the vanilla version, coordinates, resolution and performance information in the bottom-right corner.
UI_SIMBA_AutoHide_VehicleDash_Desc: Includes the vehicle dashboard in the bottom-bar animation. This setting only applies while the bottom bar animation is enabled.

UI_RSF_MO_AgingEnabled_tooltip: Characters age over time with effects on metabolism, perk caps, and recovery.

UI_RSF_MO_BackpackProtectionScale_toolti: Backpacks can block attacks from behind. Disable to remove the protection bonus.
UI_RSF_MO_BackpackProtection_tooltip: An equipped backpack can absorb a bite or scratch from behind. Military/hiking packs: 100% block. Satchels: 25%. Pack is ripped off on a block.
UI_RSF_MO_BleedDotZombies_tooltip: Allow bleed damage to finish zombies. OFF by default - the undead have no circulation, bleeding them out breaks the lore.
UI_RSF_MO_BleedEnabled_tooltip: Sharp weapons cause bleed-over-time damage and blood splatter on zombies.
UI_RSF_MO_BodyCompKey_tooltip: Hotkey to open / close the RSF Body Composition panel. Default: Numpad +.
UI_RSF_MO_BodyShapeEnabled_tooltip: Your character's body changes visually based on weight - 5 tiers: Skinny, Lean, Normal, Fat, Obese. Fat/Obese swap to full 3D meshes with matching clothing.
UI_RSF_MO_BreathHoldKey_tooltip: Hold this key to hold your breath near airborne fumes. Only used in Key Hold mode. Default: B.
UI_RSF_MO_BreathHoldMode_tooltip: How the breath-hold system works near airborne fumes. Key Hold: hold a key to hold breath. Auto: automatically holds breath near fumes. Disabled: no breath-holding.
UI_RSF_MO_BruiseEnabled_tooltip: Blunt weapons cause bruise effects that briefly slow zombies after a hit.
UI_RSF_MO_BulldozerPower_tooltip: Fat/Obese characters can sprint through and knock down zombies. Disable to remove the bulldozer ability.
UI_RSF_MO_CarryEnabled_tooltip: RSF overrides carry capacity from Strength. Disable to use vanilla carry weight or let another carry-capacity mod take over.
UI_RSF_MO_CombatDamageScale_tooltip: Enable RSF's bonus melee damage from Strength and Fitness. Disable to use vanilla damage only.
UI_RSF_MO_CrowdDensity_tooltip: Multiple zombies on the same tile slow each other (2: 65% speed; 3+: 50%). Creates natural bottlenecks at doorways. Strong zombies exempt.
UI_RSF_MO_DebugMode_tooltip: Print verbose RSF diagnostic output to the game console. Useful for tracking down bugs.
UI_RSF_MO_DirectionalCombat_tooltip: Backpedaling after a hit boosts your knockback chance. Pushing forward gives bonus crit chance and extra damage.
UI_RSF_MO_DoorBreakSlipDebug_tooltip: Shows extra debug info for the door-break slip feature. Only useful for testing.
UI_RSF_MO_DoorBreakSlip_tooltip: When a door is broken down, zombies within 2 tiles may slip on debris and fall briefly, thinning a horde at a chokepoint.
UI_RSF_MO_DoorSlipRadius_tooltip: Zombies near a broken door trip on debris. Disable to remove the trip hazard.
UI_RSF_MO_EmergencySprint_tooltip: When endurance drops to 10% or below, a 2.5-second adrenaline burst restores run capability. 30-second cooldown.
UI_RSF_MO_EnduranceOverride_tooltip: Removes the vanilla damage penalty from fatigue. A tired swing delivers full impact - physics does not care how tired you are. Attack speed penalty kept.
UI_RSF_MO_GrabEscape_tooltip: Immediately restores run/sprint when breaking free from a grab. Eliminates the ~1 second post-grab animation lock.
UI_RSF_MO_HUDScale_tooltip: Size of the heart rate / endurance HUD overlay. 1.0 = default, 1.5 = 50% larger. Applied immediately.
UI_RSF_MO_HUDUnlockKey_tooltip: Press this key to unlock the body monitor overlay for dragging. Press again to lock in place. Default: Numpad -.
UI_RSF_MO_HideDebugContext_tooltip: Hides the debug entries from the right-click context menu. Replaces the 'Disable Debug in 42' mod.
UI_RSF_MO_KnockdownDamageScale_tooltip: Knocked-down zombies take bonus damage from hitting the ground. Disable to remove all fall-damage bonuses.
UI_RSF_MO_KnockdownFall_tooltip: Knocked-down zombies take bonus damage the moment they hit the ground. Headshots on concrete can cause severe head trauma.
UI_RSF_MO_LowHealthRunners_tooltip: Zombies whose initial total health is 0.75 or lower accelerate into sprinter-style runner locomotion with sprinter growls and bites.
UI_RSF_MO_MoodlesEnabled_tooltip: Show RSF custom moodles (Heart Rate, Overtraining, Runner's High) in the MoodleFramework column. Disabling hides moodles only; all effects still apply.
UI_RSF_MO_NutritionMealOverride_tooltip: Adds extra hunger when meals are skipped, encouraging 3 meals a day for optimal muscle protein synthesis. Disable if using another hunger mod.
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_Custom_Note: The following settings are only applied when the Custom preset is selected.
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_FPSCap_tooltip: Target framerate when FPS Mode is set to Custom Cap.
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_LightingFPS_tooltip: How often the lighting system recalculates per second. Lower values improve performance.
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_Preset_desc: Potato: 40-tile render, low quality, max FPS. Normal: 72-tile render, medium quality. Master Race: 304-tile render, high quality, extended zoom. Custom: configure each setting individually below. Render distance requires the RSF class patch (IsoChunkMap.class).
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_Preset_desc_nopatch: Potato: low quality, max FPS. Normal: medium quality. Master Race: high quality, extended zoom. Custom: configure each setting individually below. Render distance is unavailable (class patch not installed).
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_Preset_tooltip: Select a performance tier. Each preset adjusts render distance, FPS, lighting, water/puddle/fog quality, and zoom levels.
UI_RSF_MO_Perf_RenderDist_tooltip: Override the chunk render distance. Requires the RSF class patch. Higher values increase CPU/GPU load significantly.
UI_RSF_MO_PivotEnabled_tooltip: Aim rotation speed depends on body weight. Lean characters pivot fastest, obese characters slowest. Replaces the external PIVOT mod.
UI_RSF_MO_QuickActions_tooltip: Speeds tedious inventory actions (pick up, wear, equip, transfer) by 2x. Mood, pain, and drunk penalties still apply.
UI_RSF_MO_RandomStartWeight_tooltip: New characters spawn with randomised body fat (10-40%) and weight (55-130 kg) instead of the fixed 22% baseline.
UI_RSF_MO_RunnerHigh_tooltip: Sustained running builds an endorphin effect that improves endurance recovery and mood. Encourages cardio-heavy playstyles.
UI_RSF_MO_SprintCollision_tooltip: Fat and Obese characters can sprint through zombies and knock them down. Heavier characters hit harder.
UI_RSF_MO_StrainRecovery_tooltip: Periodically reduces combat muscle stiffness. Fitness level scales recovery speed (Fitness 10 = 2.5x faster). Resting speeds recovery further.
UI_RSF_MO_SweatInEyes_tooltip: When overheating (vanilla Hyperthermia moodle) while exerting, sweat drips into your eyes causing temporary vision blur. Press Wipe key to clear instantly.
UI_RSF_MO_TraitSync_tooltip: Automatically assigns/removes vanilla weight traits (Underweight, Overweight, Obese) as your body tier changes. Updates on wake-up.
UI_RSF_MO_TrampleEnabled_tooltip: Crawling zombies can trip standing zombies that walk over them. Strong zombies barrel through weaker ones at +15% speed.
UI_RSF_MO_TramplePower_tooltip: Crawling zombies trip standing ones. Strong zombies bowl through weaker ones. Disable to remove these interactions.
UI_RSF_MO_VanillaXPMult_tooltip: Scales bonus XP awarded when you sleep. 1.0 = default. 0.5 = half gains. 2.0 = double gains. In Multiplayer, controlled server-side.
UI_RSF_MO_WakeSummary_tooltip: Shows the RSF sleep-conversion summary window after waking up. Disabling it mutes the popup only; XP conversion still happens immediately.
UI_RSF_MO_WeaponSwap_tooltip: Melee only. When your melee weapon breaks mid-combat, RSF equips your backup (secondary hand then back-slot) and drops the broken weapon.
UI_RSF_MO_WipeEyesKey_tooltip: Press this key to wipe sweat from your eyes during sweat-in-eyes blur. Default: E.
UI_RSF_MO_ZombieBodyShape_tooltip: Zombies use simplified body shapes: Normal, Fat, Obese. Skinny/Lean zombie visuals are folded into Normal to reduce per-zombie body-tier work.
UI_RSF_TachycardiaCollapse: Your heart skips... everything goes dark

UI_NECROA_TBS_Explanation_tt: You have your own smell, at some point, the zombies will use that to track you, be aware
UI_NECROA_TT_AB: Anabolic Boost - testosterone or something similar floods their system. Some of them get huge, way heavier than normal
UI_NECROA_TT_AE: Acute Encephalopathy - brain damage. Most don't make it. Neurological collapse, death in most cases (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_AP: Ambush Predation - the reanimated ones play dead. Stay still, wait for you to get close. Double-tap everything
UI_NECROA_TT_AR: Acid Reflux - their saliva burns. Extreme reflux, acid from the stomach. Don't let them spit on you (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_AS: Adrenal Surge - their adrenal glands go haywire. Adrenaline nonstop. They're more alert, more aggressive
UI_NECROA_TT_Air_Icon: Air 1 - it gets into the lungs and bypasses something. Heard a doc say alveolar something. Breathing near them is risky
UI_NECROA_TT_Air_Icon2: Air 2 - the virus travels on dust particles. Humid air, crowded places, bad news
UI_NECROA_TT_Air_Icon3: Air 3 - when their heads pop, the mist carries it. Stay back when they go down
UI_NECROA_TT_Anaerobic_Resuscitation_Ico: Anaerobic Resuscitation - apparently the cells in their brains don't need oxygen anymore. They use some chemical reaction I don't really understand. Lactic acid or something. Whatever's left of the person is gone
UI_NECROA_TT_Autophagia: Autophagia - they eat themselves. Fingers, skin. The virus drives them to it (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Autothysis: Autothysis - gas builds up inside them. Hydrogen sulphide and methane. They can explode when hit hard
UI_NECROA_TT_BD: Bone Dysplasia - their bones get denser. More protection. Like they're wearing a second skeleton
UI_NECROA_TT_Bat_Icon: Bat 1 - bats are carriers now. Avoid caves and attics (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Bat_Iconblack: Bat 2 - infected bats swarm at night. They go for the face, heard it from a guy who barely made it (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Bird_Icon: Bird 1 - apparently the virus jumped to birds. Saw infected ones acting strange, attacking people (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Bird_Iconblack: Bird 2 - something changed in the infected birds. They swarm and attack in groups now, like they're coordinated (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Blood_Icon: Blood 1 - blood contact spreads it now. Whatever gets into the bloodstream, stays there
UI_NECROA_TT_Blood_Icon2: Blood 2 - the virus multiplies directly in the blood. Even a small cut can be enough
UI_NECROA_TT_CE: Cranial Elephantitis - their skulls grow. Bone tumors or something. Thicker heads, harder to put down
UI_NECROA_TT_CM: Cranial Metastasis - neurons develop in the lungs somehow. Some headless corpses get back up. I've seen it
UI_NECROA_TT_CR1: Cold Resistance 1 - cold doesn't kill it anymore. Survives freezing, refrigerators, winter (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_CR2: Cold Resistance 2 - extreme cold doesn't work. It evolved. We're running out of ways to destroy it (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_CS: Cathermeral Shift - their eyes adapt to bright light. Sun doesn't slow them down as much
UI_NECROA_TT_Cannibalism: Cannibalism - the infected start eating human flesh. The hunger takes over (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Coma: Coma - brain inflammation. Some infected just collapse, lose consciousness. Don't know if they ever wake up (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Cytopathic_Reanimation_Icon: Cytopathic Reanimation - something in the cells lets the dead get back up. Neural structures reforming, I read that somewhere. Dead turns into one of them
UI_NECROA_TT_DC: Dermal Calcification - calcium builds up in their skin. Like armor. Harder to cut through
UI_NECROA_TT_DF: Drifting Fermentation - they bloat. Decomposition is controlled somehow. They float on water (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_DM: Dyskinetic Movement - involuntary twitches keep them in sync. Weird to watch. They move as a unit (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_DR: Autolytic Delay - something slows their decay. Digestive enzymes in the cells don't work right. They last longer (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_DR1: Drug Resistance 1 - the antivirals don't work anymore. Class 1 and 2, whatever that means. We're running out of options
UI_NECROA_TT_DR2: Drug Resistance 2 - even the stronger antivirals fail. Class 3 and 4. The cure gets harder every day
UI_NECROA_TT_ED: Epidermal Digestion - enzymes break down their own skin for nutrients. Severely damaged corpses can still reanimate
UI_NECROA_TT_EMC: Enhanced Motor Control - their movements are smoother, faster. Like the virus rewired their motor cortex or something
UI_NECROA_TT_EQ: Engorded Quadriceps - nutrients get pulled from the rest of the corpse into the legs. They sacrifice the body to move the horde faster
UI_NECROA_TT_ES: Enhanced Sensory Integration - nutrients flow to the parts of the brain that handle sight and hearing. They see and hear better than they should
UI_NECROA_TT_Echopraxia: Echopraxia - they copy each other's movements. Frontal lobe damage, I think. They navigate obstacles better in groups (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Fever: Fever - high fever, weakness. Their body is fighting something it can't win (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_GH: Genetic Hardening - the virus is harder to analyze. Lab work takes longer. Something in its structure changed (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_GR1: Genetic Reshuffle 1 - the pathogen's DNA reassembled. Different structure. More work to find a cure
UI_NECROA_TT_GR2: Genetic Reshuffle 2 - a new strain exists. Completely different. Starting from scratch on the cure (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Gastroenteritis: Gastroenteritis - stomach and gut go wrong. They vomit constantly. And it's contagious (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Genome_Icon: Segmented Genome - the virus split its genetic material into smaller parts. Makes it mutate faster, harder to track (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HI: Horde Instinct - the hordes move with purpose. Cross land, cross water. They're heading somewhere (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HI1: Horde Mentality - they stick together. One moves, the rest follow. Pack behavior (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HP: Horde Pheromones - the hordes give off chemicals. Pheromones. Others are drawn to them (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HR1: Heat Resistance 1 - it's learning to survive heat. Normal temperatures don't faze it (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HR2: Heat Resistance 2 - extreme heat doesn't kill it. Fire, boiling, nothing. It adapts (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HS: Hyper Salivation - something's wrong with their throat. They drool constantly. Saliva everywhere (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_HV: Horde Vocalisation - the leaders make distinct sounds. Moans that draw others in. Like a beacon
UI_NECROA_TT_Hyperosmia: Hyperosmia - their sense of smell gets way worse. Or better, for them. They can track you by scent
UI_NECROA_TT_Insect_Icon: Insect - even insects can get infected now. Not sure how that works biologically (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Insomnia: Insomnia - they can't sleep. Or won't. Exhaustion, fatigue. Still coming for you though (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_LH: Lumbrical Hypertrophy - the muscles in their hands get bigger. Once they grab you, good luck breaking free
UI_NECROA_TT_LN: Liquefactive Necrosis - their organs are half-liquid. Rupture easy. Hit the right spot and they pop
UI_NECROA_TT_LR: Liquefactive Resistance - their insides don't liquefy as quick. Enzymes get denatured or something. Decomposition slowed (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_MT: Masticatory Tension - jaw muscles are way stronger. They bite through thick clothing, leather, everything
UI_NECROA_TT_Mummification: Mummification - the badly decayed ones can hibernate. Shut down, wait. Don't assume they're dead (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_NM: Naja Mortis - muscles grew around their jaw. They can spit at you from a distance, like some kind of venom (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Nausea_Icon: Gastrointestinal Expansion - stomach and intestines. Vomit and feces are contagious. Disgusting (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_PR: Putrefactive Resistance - bacteria can't break them down as fast. Proteins stay intact. They rot slower (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_PS: Peptide Surge - something in their blood makes them stronger. Peptides, hormones, I'm not sure. They hit harder
UI_NECROA_TT_Paranoia: Delirium - irrationality, paranoia. They don't think straight. Makes them unpredictable (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_PhotophobiaIcon: Photophobia - their eyes get sensitive. Sunlight hurts them. At least that gives us something (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Polyphagia: Polyphagia - compulsive hunger. They can't stop eating. Or trying to (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Psychosis: Psychosis - the infected have psychotic breaks. Violent, unpredictable. Like something broke in their head (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_RA: Regenerative Activation - some of the dead get back up. Nerves regenerate in the brain. Don't assume they're done
UI_NECROA_TT_RB: Regenerative Bio-Synthesis - even with bad head wounds they can come back. Proteins regenerate the brain. Nothing stays down
UI_NECROA_TT_Rodent_Icon: Rodent 1 - rats can carry it now. Found infected ones in the sewers (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Rodent_Iconblack: Rodent 2 - infected rats hunt in packs. They go for the ankles, nasty little things (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_ST: Structured Travel - they follow leaders. The horde moves in one direction, faster than they should (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Saliva_Icon: Saliva 1 - their saliva is loaded with it. Salivary glands produce way more than normal
UI_NECROA_TT_Saliva_Icon2: Saliva 2 - nasal mucus too now. Snot, spit, anything from the face. Keep your distance
UI_NECROA_TT_TL: Temporal Lobe Manipulation - they're drawn to movement. Once you're dead they lose interest. More people turn instead of getting eaten (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_Urogenital_Icon: Urogenital Expansion - it replicates in kidneys and urinary tract. Bodily fluids, you know (Not implemented)
UI_NECROA_TT_VH: Vampiric Hunger - they go for the blood, not the flesh. Bite and suck. Victims often turn instead of dying
UI_NECROA_TT_Water_Icon: Water 1 - the virus survives in fresh water. Ponds, rain, humid air. Don't drink untreated
UI_NECROA_TT_Water_Icon2: Water 2 - even treated water isn't safe anymore. Chlorine doesn't kill it. Boil everything
UI_NECROA_TT_Zoonotic_Icon: Zoonotic Shift - the virus seems to be mutating to infect different species. Heard it makes it harder to predict and contain (Not implemented)

UI_AMS_Help_Breathing: Breathing: Respirators, gas masks, and other sealed headgear restrict airflow. This adds to your exertion cost during physical activity. The severity is shown as Mildly Restricted, Restricted, or Heavily Restricted depending on the gear.
UI_AMS_Help_Burden: Burden: The total physical weight and bulk of your worn armor. The bar shows your current load on a fixed scale. Heavier loadouts drain endurance faster during running, sprinting, and melee combat. In heavy armor, your arms also tire faster per swing.
UI_AMS_Help_CostDrivers: Cost Drivers: Shows which worn items contribute most to your total burden, sorted by impact. If one item dominates the list, swapping it out will make the biggest difference.
UI_AMS_Help_ExportTitleDesc: Support Reports: If something feels wrong, use this to save a snapshot of your current loadout, burden calculations, mod list, and game state to a text file. Attach it when reporting a problem.
UI_AMS_Help_Overview: Overview: Armor costs scale with activity. Standing still or walking costs almost nothing. Running, sprinting, and fighting is where heavy armor makes itself felt. The heavier your outfit, the faster you tire during exertion and the slower you recover afterward.
UI_AMS_Help_Sleep: Sleep: Sleeping in rigid armor slows fatigue recovery. The exact effect depends on your fatigue, bed quality, traits, and sandbox settings. Take off rigid gear before bed.
UI_AMS_Help_Thermal: Thermal: Insulating gear adds exertion cost only after your body remains hot long enough. Short temperature spikes fade without a penalty. In cold conditions, Helpful means the insulation suits the weather; AMS does not add a cold bonus. Vanilla clothing condition and wetness are included in the reading.

UI_SlowBurn_Note_Text: Day 3 since the bite. Still thinking clearly. They don't attack me anymore - they think I'm one of them. Must be careful. Any sudden movements or loud noises and they realize what I am. <LINE> <LINE> The wound won't heal but it doesn't hurt. I should be dead by now. Why am I still alive? <LINE> <LINE> If you find this and I'm gone, know that I tried to stay human as long as I could.
UI_SlowBurn_WelcomeText: <CENTRE> <SIZE:large> Slow Burn </SIZE> </CENTRE> <LINE> You are infected, but you never turned. As long as you keep your cover, the dead will leave you be. <LINE> <LINE> <SIZE:medium> Suspicion </SIZE> <LINE> Zombies judge you by how you act, not just how you look. Running, fighting, and loud noises raise your Suspicion through five stages: Hidden, Suspicious, Exposed, Hunted, Blown. Stay calm, move slowly, and it decays back down over time. <LINE> <LINE> <SIZE:medium> Naked Hordes </SIZE> <LINE> Occasionally a naked horde passes by, led by a smart one that can see through your disguise. Spotted, it sets the whole pack on you. Keep your distance and let it pass. <LINE> <LINE> <SIZE:medium> Fever </SIZE> <LINE> Your infection is slowly burning hotter. Herbal remedies and medicine slow it down - left unchecked, it eventually turns terminal. <LINE> <LINE> <SIZE:medium> Controls </SIZE> <LINE> TAB - toggle the suspicion / fever HUD <LINE> Z - devour a nearby corpse (crouch first) - resets suspicion, spikes fever <LINE> G - cover yourself in zombie remains for a temporary disguise boost <LINE> N - toggle zombie-walk mode, shamble like the dead to help sell it <LINE> V - groan like the dead to reduce Suspicion a little (has a cooldown) <LINE> <LINE> All of these can be rebound under Options -> Controls, in their own "Slow Burn" section. <LINE> <LINE> Keep an eye on that HUD, and good luck out there.

UI_FindAlice_FinalNote_Text: To whoever finds this place, <LINE> <LINE> If you've read my diary, you know how I got here. Ten days that felt like a lifetime. <LINE> <LINE> I left my pendant on the porch. Dad gave it to me. Said the stone inside had a little light that would never go out, 'just like you, Alice.' <LINE> <LINE> I want someone else to carry it now. Wherever you're going, take it with you. Keep it in your pocket. When it gets really dark -- and it will -- hold it up. It still glows. I promise. <LINE> <LINE> Thank you for following my story. Thank you for not giving up. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Hint1: Alice loved volleyball. She spent her summers at the camp on the lakeshore
UI_FindAlice_Hint10: They headed to the airport near Louisville at first light
UI_FindAlice_Hint2: She headed south from the camp. Look near the water treatment plant
UI_FindAlice_Hint3: She heard about survivors at the church in Irvington
UI_FindAlice_Hint4: She stopped at a gas station on the way north
UI_FindAlice_Hint5: She went to her Aunt May's farm near Ekron
UI_FindAlice_Hint6: A radio broadcast led her to a station west of Riverside
UI_FindAlice_Hint7: The group stopped at a supermarket in West Point
UI_FindAlice_Hint8: They searched the mall for supplies before Louisville
UI_FindAlice_Hint9: They found shelter at a market near the city
UI_FindAlice_Obj_AllFound: Find Alice's refuge in the woods
UI_FindAlice_Page10_Text: July 18 <LINE> <LINE> We didn't make it. <LINE> <LINE> The noise from the planes drew them in from everywhere. The fences were down. We watched the last plane take off from half a mile out. Just... lift off. Gone. <LINE> <LINE> The group fell apart after that. Some headed for the coast. The lieutenant told everyone to make for high ground. His voice cracked for the first time. <LINE> <LINE> I don't know what happened to Claire. I hope she made it. <LINE> <LINE> I walked south all day. Alone again. But I know where I'm going. <LINE> <LINE> My grandparents' cabin, east of Muldraugh. Small, hidden in the woods. Nobody will think to look there. <LINE> <LINE> I'll wait. Someone will come. They have to. <LINE> <LINE> The stone on my pendant has been glowing brighter lately. It gets stronger when they're close. I don't know how, but it does. It's like Dad's still protecting me somehow. <LINE> <LINE> If anyone finds this -- I made it this far. That has to count for something, right? <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page1_Text: July 9 <LINE> <LINE> Something terrible happened today. We were at the camp by the lake, south of March Ridge. It was supposed to be the best week of the summer. I'd just won the volleyball match this morning. <LINE> <LINE> After lunch, the counselors started acting strange. Mr. Davies grabbed Jenny by the arm and bit her. She wouldn't stop screaming. Then more of them turned. Everyone was running. <LINE> <LINE> They told us to stay in our cabins. I could hear everything through the thin walls. The screaming went on for hours. Then it just... stopped. That was worse. Way worse. <LINE> <LINE> Something strange happened while I was hiding. The stone on my pendant -- the one Dad gave me -- started glowing. It's never done that before. Just a faint light, barely there. But in that darkness, it felt like Dad was with me. <LINE> <LINE> More of them kept coming from the north, from the town. I slipped out at first light with my backpack, heading south along the lake. I have to find Dad. He'll know what's going on -- he always does. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page2_Text: July 10 <LINE> <LINE> I kept going south from the camp. Found an old water treatment plant by the lake. The place reeks and the tanks are full of stagnant water, but at least it's quiet. Nobody comes here. <LINE> <LINE> I slept behind one of the big tanks with my backpack as a pillow. Not exactly the camp beds I'm used to. <LINE> <LINE> This morning I met someone on the road. An old guy with a hunting rifle. My hands were shaking but he just lowered it and said 'You shouldn't be out here alone, kid.' Understatement of the century. <LINE> <LINE> He told me people are gathering at a church in Irvington. West of here. Safety in numbers, he said. <LINE> <LINE> Irvington. Maybe someone there has news. Maybe someone's seen Dad. <LINE> <LINE> I'm going. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page3_Text: July 11 <LINE> <LINE> Made it to the church in Irvington. There are people here -- not many, maybe five or six. They have a car and they're planning to drive south on the interstate tomorrow. As far from the cities as possible. <LINE> <LINE> They asked me to come. Part of me wanted to say yes so badly. They had food, blankets, a plan. But Dad is north. The facility is north. And if anyone understands what's happening, it's him. <LINE> <LINE> So I said no. <LINE> <LINE> I'll head to Aunt May's farm near Ekron. She's Dad's sister and she's the toughest person I know. Once chased a wolf off with a frying pan. At least that's how she tells it. <LINE> <LINE> It's a long way north. I'll need to find food along the way -- gas stations, stores, whatever I can find on the road. <LINE> <LINE> I leave at dawn. Alone again. But it's okay. I think. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page4_Text: July 12 <LINE> <LINE> Stopped at a gas station on the road north. I was so thirsty I could barely think. <LINE> <LINE> There was a man inside. He pointed a shotgun at me before I even said hello. Told me to get out. His hands were shaking worse than mine. <LINE> <LINE> I think he was more scared than I was. He'd pushed a refrigerator against the door and there were empty cans everywhere. He must have been in there for days. <LINE> <LINE> He let me take some water and a box of crackers before I left. Didn't say goodbye. Just watched me go through the window. <LINE> <LINE> Aunt May's farm can't be far now. I just have to keep walking. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page5_Text: July 13 <LINE> <LINE> Aunt May is alive. <LINE> <LINE> When she opened the door and saw me she didn't say a word. She just pulled me in and held on. We stood there in the doorway for a long time. She smells like hay and wood smoke, same as always. <LINE> <LINE> Uncle Bill went out hunting with a friend last week and never came back. She tried the old radio but nobody answers anymore. Just static and silence. <LINE> <LINE> She wants to stay. Says these walls have kept her safe this long and she's too old to start running. I tried to argue but she just made me tea and said 'Some people run toward the storm, Alice. You always have.' <LINE> <LINE> She's right, I guess. I'm still looking for Dad. <LINE> <LINE> I picked up a radio broadcast before bed. Faint, crackling, but clear enough: survivors should head to the radio station west of Riverside. That's where I'm going. <LINE> <LINE> I left Aunt May her favorite tea in the cupboard. It's all I had to give. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page6_Text: July 14 <LINE> <LINE> I found the radio station. There are people everywhere -- well, maybe twenty, but it feels like a city after being alone so long. <LINE> <LINE> There's a lieutenant organizing everything. Calm voice, steady hands. He's been gathering survivors for days. He says we're moving east tomorrow, toward the airport near Louisville. A flight out. An actual plan. <LINE> <LINE> But first we need supplies. West Point has a supermarket that might still have food. So we go there first. <LINE> <LINE> I sat by the fire tonight and someone handed me a can of peaches. I almost cried. Not because of the peaches. Because someone thought to share. <LINE> <LINE> For the first time since the camp, I feel like things might be okay. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page7_Text: July 15 <LINE> <LINE> We spent the night at the supermarket in West Point. More people joined us on the road. There must be thirty of us now. <LINE> <LINE> Bad news though. The bridge into Louisville is crawling with them. We can hear them from here, this low groaning sound that doesn't stop. The lieutenant says we'll go around -- try the mall south of the city first for supplies, then find another way to the airport. <LINE> <LINE> A woman named Claire taught me how to wrap a sprained ankle tonight. I don't have a sprained ankle but she said everyone should know. She used to be a nurse. Now she carries a baseball bat and still calls everyone 'sweetie.' <LINE> <LINE> I'm scared of tomorrow. But I'm not alone anymore. That counts for something. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page8_Text: July 16 <LINE> <LINE> The mall was bad. We found supplies on the south end but the north side... we could hear them through the walls. Hundreds. Maybe more. <LINE> <LINE> We grabbed what we could and got out fast. Nobody talked much after. <LINE> <LINE> If the mall is like that, I don't want to think about Louisville. <LINE> <LINE> One of the guys from the group knows a produce market nearby. Off the main roads, easy to miss. He says we can spend the night there without being noticed. Tomorrow we push for the airport. <LINE> <LINE> It has to work. It just has to. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_Page9_Text: July 17 <LINE> <LINE> We made it to the market. Everyone. All of us. <LINE> <LINE> I'm sitting on the roof right now, writing by moonlight. From here I can hear the planes. They're still flying -- the low rumble comes and goes, and sometimes I catch their blinking lights against the clouds. They're still getting people out. <LINE> <LINE> Tomorrow morning we head straight for the airport. Together. Quiet. Fast. <LINE> <LINE> Tomorrow I'll be on a plane. Tomorrow the sky will carry us somewhere safe and I'll find Dad on the other side. He probably made it out ages ago. He's probably worried sick. I bet he's pacing. <LINE> <LINE> The stars are out tonight. Mom used to say each one was someone watching over us. I hope she's watching now. <LINE> <LINE> - Alice
UI_FindAlice_ScientistNote_Text: If you're reading this, I'm already gone. I don't have much time so I'll be brief. <LINE> <LINE> My name is Viktor Holm. I was a researcher at the Rosewood facility. I helped create what they're calling the Knox Event. I won't ask for forgiveness. I don't deserve it. <LINE> <LINE> But Alice does. My daughter. She's 14, she has her mother's eyes and she's braver than I ever was. She was at the summer camp south of March Ridge when it all started. I tried to get to her. The roads were already gone. <LINE> <LINE> Alice writes everything down. She's kept a diary since her mother passed. If she made it out, she'll have left a trail. Her words, scattered behind her like breadcrumbs. <LINE> <LINE> Please. Find her pages. Follow her story. Maybe she's still out there. <LINE> <LINE> And if you find her -- tell her Dad's sorry he was late. Tell her the pendant still glows. <LINE> <LINE> - V.H.

UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Advanced_P1: Long-term food security requires seed saving and season extension. These advanced techniques free you from dependence on scavenged seed packets and short growing seasons.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Advanced_P2: Seed saving starts with understanding pollination. Open-pollinated varieties produce seeds that grow true to type. Hybrid varieties (marked F1 on packets) do not — their seeds produce unpredictable offspring. Save seeds only from open-pollinated plants, and allow them to fully mature on the plant before harvesting.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Advanced_P3: To save tomato seeds, scoop them into water and let them ferment for two to three days. The gel coating dissolves and viable seeds sink while debris floats. Rinse and dry them thoroughly before storage. Store seeds in a cool, dark, dry place — a sealed jar with a desiccant packet works well.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Advanced_P4: Cold frames extend the growing season by weeks. A simple cold frame is a bottomless box with a transparent lid (glass or clear plastic) placed over a garden bed. Sunlight heats the air inside while the frame blocks wind and retains warmth overnight. Vent the frame on warm days to prevent overheating.

UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Beginner_P1: Farming provides a renewable food source that doesn't depend on scavenging dwindling supplies. Even a small garden can supplement your diet with fresh vegetables and herbs.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Beginner_P2: Good soil is the foundation of successful farming. Plants need nutrients, water retention, and drainage. Sandy soil drains too quickly and holds few nutrients. Clay soil retains water but can suffocate roots. The ideal garden soil is loamy — a mix of sand, silt, and clay with organic matter mixed in.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Beginner_P3: Seeds need three things to germinate: moisture, warmth, and contact with soil. Plant seeds at the depth recommended for their type — generally two to three times the seed's diameter. Too deep and the sprout can't reach sunlight. Too shallow and it dries out.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Beginner_P4: Watering should be deep but infrequent. Shallow daily watering encourages roots to stay near the surface where they're vulnerable. A deep soaking every few days encourages roots to grow downward toward moisture, creating stronger, more drought-resistant plants.

UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Intermediate_P1: Managing a growing garden requires knowledge of plant diseases, pests, and nutrient management. Healthy plants resist problems better than stressed ones.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Intermediate_P2: Crop rotation prevents soil depletion. Different plants use different nutrients — planting the same crop in the same spot year after year depletes specific nutrients while leaving others untouched. Rotate between heavy feeders (tomatoes, corn), light feeders (herbs, root vegetables), and nitrogen fixers (beans, peas).
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Intermediate_P3: Common garden pests include aphids, caterpillars, and slugs. Aphids cluster on new growth and suck plant juices. Caterpillars chew leaves and can strip a plant overnight. Slugs feed at night and leave silvery trails. Hand-picking pests and encouraging natural predators (birds, ladybugs) are the most practical controls.
UI_Lesson_Agriculture_Intermediate_P4: Composting turns kitchen scraps and yard waste into rich fertilizer. Alternate layers of green material (food scraps, fresh grass) and brown material (dried leaves, cardboard). Turn the pile regularly to provide oxygen. A working compost pile generates heat and breaks down material in weeks to months.

UI_Lesson_Aiming_Advanced_P1: Advanced marksmanship tackles the variables that make distant and low-visibility shots difficult: bullet drop, wind drift, and diminished sight pictures.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Advanced_P2: Bullet drop increases with distance. A bullet begins falling the instant it leaves the barrel. At close range the drop is negligible, but at 100 meters or beyond you must aim above the target to compensate. Scope elevation adjustments or holdover techniques account for this predictable arc.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Advanced_P3: Wind pushes a bullet sideways during flight. Estimating wind speed and direction is one of the hardest marksmanship skills. Observe environmental cues: grass movement, dust, flags, and the feel on your face. A steady 10 mph crosswind can push a bullet several inches off target at moderate range.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Advanced_P4: Low-light shooting challenges your sight picture. Tritium night sights glow faintly in darkness, providing visible aim points without batteries. Flashlight-mounted weapons illuminate the target but also reveal your position. The key principle: never shoot at something you haven't positively identified.

UI_Lesson_Aiming_Beginner_P1: Accurate shooting starts long before you pull the trigger. The fundamentals of aiming apply to every firearm, from a small pistol to a full-length rifle. Mastering these basics dramatically improves your chance of hitting what you intend to.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Beginner_P2: Sight alignment is the foundation. Line up the front sight inside the rear sight notch so the top of the front post sits level with the top of the rear. Your eye should focus on the front sight, not the target — the target will be slightly blurry, and that is correct. Trying to focus on everything at once leads to missed shots.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Beginner_P3: Trigger control is equally critical. Squeeze the trigger slowly and steadily with the pad of your index finger. Jerking or slapping the trigger pulls the gun off target at the exact moment it fires. The shot should almost surprise you when it breaks.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Beginner_P4: Breathing affects aim more than most beginners realize. Take a natural breath, exhale halfway, and pause — this respiratory pause is your most stable moment. Shoot during this pause. Holding your breath too long causes tremors that worsen accuracy.

UI_Lesson_Aiming_Intermediate_P1: Once the fundamentals are solid, accuracy depends on your shooting position. A stable platform absorbs recoil and keeps sights on target between shots.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Intermediate_P2: The Isosceles stance is the most natural for beginners: face the target squarely, feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended equally forming an isosceles triangle. Lean slightly forward at the waist to manage recoil. The Weaver stance angles the body, using push-pull tension between the arms — it offers better recoil control but takes practice.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Intermediate_P3: Shooting from behind cover is a survival essential. Expose as little of your body as possible. Brace the weapon against the edge of cover for stability, but never rest the barrel directly on a hard surface — it throws off your point of impact. Use your support hand or a soft rest between the gun and the surface.
UI_Lesson_Aiming_Intermediate_P4: Moving targets require leading — aiming ahead of the target's direction of travel so the bullet and the target arrive at the same point. The faster the target moves or the farther away it is, the more lead is required. Swing the barrel smoothly to match the target's speed and continue the swing through the trigger pull.

UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Advanced_P1: Advanced animal care involves performing basic veterinary procedures, managing herd genetics over multiple generations, and maximizing sustainable production.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Advanced_P2: Assisting difficult births (dystocia) is the most critical veterinary skill. Signs of trouble include prolonged labor without progress, abnormal presentation (legs or tail first instead of head), and maternal distress. Gentle repositioning of the offspring and careful traction during contractions can save both mother and young. Hygiene is critical — clean hands and clean instruments prevent post-birth infection.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Advanced_P3: Hoof trimming prevents lameness in cattle, sheep, and goats. Overgrown hooves cause pain and abnormal gait. Use sharp hoof shears to trim back to the natural shape, removing excess growth from the walls and sole. Trim on a flat surface to check for level. Trim too deep and you hit the quick, causing bleeding and pain.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Advanced_P4: Sustainable herd management balances breeding rate against available resources. Overbreeding depletes pasture and feed stores, leading to malnourished animals that produce less. Calculate carrying capacity: how many animals can your land and stored feed support through the worst season? Breed to maintain that number, culling excess stock for meat rather than stretching resources thin.

UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Beginner_P1: Keeping livestock provides a renewable source of food, materials, and labor. Chickens produce eggs, cows give milk, and sheep provide wool. Proper care keeps animals healthy and productive.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Beginner_P2: Every animal needs three basics: food, water, and shelter. Chickens eat grain, scraps, and insects. Cows and sheep need pasture grass or hay. Pigs are omnivores that eat almost anything. Fresh water must be available at all times — a dehydrated animal stops producing and sickens rapidly.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Beginner_P3: Shelter protects livestock from weather and predators. A simple three-sided shed with a roof stops wind and rain. Fencing keeps animals contained and predators out. Chicken wire works for poultry but larger animals need sturdy fencing — wire, wood, or a combination.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Beginner_P4: Observe your animals daily. Changes in behavior, appetite, or appearance signal health problems early. A chicken that stops eating, a cow that separates from the herd, or a sheep with matted wool all indicate issues that worsen without intervention.

UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Intermediate_P1: Intermediate animal husbandry covers breeding programs, optimized feeding, and recognizing and treating common livestock diseases.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Intermediate_P2: Breeding requires a healthy male and female of breeding age. Most livestock breed seasonally — sheep in autumn, chickens year-round. Select breeding stock based on desirable traits: high egg production, strong build, calm temperament. Inbreeding weakens offspring, so maintain genetic diversity by trading animals with other survivors when possible.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Intermediate_P3: Feed quality directly affects production. Laying hens need extra calcium (crushed eggshells or oyster shell) for strong eggshells. Milking cows need high-quality forage and supplemental grain for sustained output. Underfeeding reduces production long before visible weight loss appears.
UI_Lesson_AnimalCare_Intermediate_P4: Common livestock diseases include respiratory infections (coughing, nasal discharge), parasites (weight loss despite eating, visible worms), and foot rot (limping, foul-smelling hooves). Quarantine sick animals immediately to prevent spread. Basic treatments include wound cleaning, keeping the animal warm and hydrated, and natural antiparasitic plants like garlic and wormwood.

UI_Lesson_Axe_Advanced_P1: An advanced axe user maintains their tool in peak condition and adapts their technique to unusual situations including thrown strikes and using the axe as a breaching tool.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Advanced_P2: Sharpening an axe requires a file or whetstone. File into the edge, not away from it, maintaining the existing bevel angle — typically 25 to 30 degrees. A convex grind (slightly rounded edge profile) resists chipping better than a flat grind. After filing, hone with a whetstone for a razor edge.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Advanced_P3: Throwing an axe is a desperation tactic but useful to know. Grip the handle at the base, raise overhead, and release as your arm reaches full extension. One full rotation occurs at roughly five meters — practice at that distance first. The risk is obvious: a missed throw leaves you unarmed.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Advanced_P4: As a breaching tool, strike door hinges and lock areas rather than the center of a door. The lock and hinges are the weakest points. Alternate between the blade edge for cutting through wood and the flat poll (back of the head) for hammering. This dual use preserves the cutting edge for combat.

UI_Lesson_Axe_Beginner_P1: The axe is one of the most versatile melee weapons in a survival situation. It chops wood, breaches doors, and dispatches threats. Proper handling keeps you effective and prevents self-injury.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Beginner_P2: Grip the axe with your dominant hand near the head and your other hand at the base of the handle. As you swing, let the top hand slide down to meet the bottom hand — this adds speed and power while maintaining control. Never choke up with both hands near the head, as this limits your swing arc.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Beginner_P3: The power of an axe comes from its arc, not brute strength. Let gravity and centrifugal force do the work. A smooth, controlled overhead swing generates more impact than a short, muscled chop. Aim for a specific spot — accuracy matters more than force.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Beginner_P4: Safety means awareness. Before swinging, check for overhead obstructions, people behind you, and your own footing. An axe that glances off its target carries lethal momentum. Keep the blade sharp — a dull axe bounces and deflects unpredictably.

UI_Lesson_Axe_Intermediate_P1: Using an axe effectively in combat requires understanding distance, timing, and where to strike for maximum effect.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Intermediate_P2: The axe's greatest advantage is reach. A full-length axe keeps threats at arm's length plus the handle length. Maintain this distance — if an attacker closes inside your swing arc, the axe head passes behind them and you're left exposed. Step back to reset distance rather than shortening your swing.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Intermediate_P3: Target the head and neck for immediate incapacitation. Against the undead, the skull is the only reliable target. A horizontal swing to the temple has the widest margin for error. Overhead chops to the crown are powerful but require precise aim. Avoid swinging at limbs — it wastes energy without stopping the threat.
UI_Lesson_Axe_Intermediate_P4: Recovery matters. After each swing, return to a guard position with the axe head between you and the threat. An axe committed too deep into a target can get stuck, leaving you weaponless. Use controlled swings that penetrate enough to be lethal without burying the blade.

UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Advanced_P1: Advanced blacksmithing produces functional tools — knives, chisels, punches, and hardware — using heat treatment to achieve the right balance of hardness and toughness.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Advanced_P2: Forging a knife starts with high-carbon steel — old leaf springs, files, and railroad spikes are excellent salvage sources. Draw out the blade profile, forge the bevels by hammering at an angle, and form the tang (the extension that goes into the handle). Refine the shape with a grinder before heat treatment.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Advanced_P3: Hardening requires heating the blade to critical temperature — when it becomes non-magnetic (test with a magnet). Quench in oil for a controlled hardening rate. Water quench is faster but risks cracking. The blade is now glass-hard but brittle.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Advanced_P4: Tempering reduces brittleness. Clean the blade surface to bare metal and heat it slowly in an oven or over coals. Watch the oxide colors that appear: straw yellow at 220 degrees Celsius for razors, bronze at 260 for knives, blue at 300 for springs. When the desired color reaches the edge, quench immediately to lock in that temper.

UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Beginner_P1: Blacksmithing transforms raw metal into tools, weapons, and hardware using heat and hammer. It is one of the oldest crafts and among the most valuable in a world where manufactured goods are no longer produced.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Beginner_P2: A forge is any setup that can heat metal to working temperature — roughly 900 to 1100 degrees Celsius for mild steel, when the metal glows bright orange to yellow. A coal or charcoal forge is the simplest to build: a fire pit with forced air from a bellows or blower, and a way to contain the heat.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Beginner_P3: The essential tools are a hammer, an anvil (or any heavy flat steel surface), and tongs to hold hot metal. A quench bucket of water or oil cools finished pieces. Without tongs you cannot safely manipulate glowing steel — bare hands and pliers are not substitutes.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Beginner_P4: Safety is paramount. Hot metal looks the same as cold metal once it drops below a visible glow — always assume metal near the forge is hot. Wear leather gloves, a leather apron, and eye protection. Sparks and scale fly unpredictably during hammering. Keep water nearby for burns and fire suppression.

UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Intermediate_P1: The three fundamental forging operations — drawing out, upsetting, and bending — form the basis of nearly every blacksmithing project.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Intermediate_P2: Drawing out makes metal longer and thinner. Heat the workpiece and hammer it on the anvil face, rotating it 90 degrees between sets of blows to keep the cross-section even. This is how bar stock is tapered into points for hooks, chisels, and nail rod. Work from the tip back toward the body of the piece.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Intermediate_P3: Upsetting is the opposite — making metal shorter and thicker by hammering on the end. Heat only the section you want to thicken and strike the end against the anvil or with the hammer. This technique creates bolt heads, decorative knobs, and reinforced striking surfaces.
UI_Lesson_Blacksmithing_Intermediate_P4: Bending uses the anvil horn or edge to curve heated metal. Place the workpiece so the bend point sits at the anvil edge, then hammer the overhanging portion downward. For tight curves, use the horn. For gentle arcs, bend gradually over a wider form. Always bend with the grain of the metal to avoid cracking.

UI_Lesson_Butchering_Advanced_P1: Advanced butchering wastes nothing. Bones, fat, sinew, and organs all have uses beyond the obvious meat cuts.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Advanced_P2: Rendering fat produces tallow (from beef or sheep) or lard (from pigs). Cut fat into small cubes, heat slowly in a pot until the fat melts and the solid bits (cracklings) float and turn golden. Strain through cloth into jars. Rendered fat stores for months without refrigeration and serves as cooking oil, candle material, soap base, and leather conditioner.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Advanced_P3: Bones simmered for hours produce bone broth — a nutrient-rich liquid packed with minerals, gelatin, and amino acids. Roast bones first for deeper flavor. After extracting broth, dried bones can be ground into bone meal fertilizer for gardens or carved into tools and buttons.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Advanced_P4: Sinew (tendons) dried and split into fibers makes some of the strongest natural cordage available. It was used for bowstrings, thread, and lashing for thousands of years. Remove tendons from the legs, strip the membrane, and dry them thoroughly. When needed, soak a strip in water until pliable, then use it as thread or binding — it shrinks as it dries, creating an incredibly tight bond.

UI_Lesson_Butchering_Beginner_P1: Butchering converts a whole animal into usable meat, hide, and bone. Proper technique maximizes yield and prevents contamination that makes meat unsafe to eat.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Beginner_P2: Field dressing — removing the internal organs — must happen as soon as possible after the kill. Body heat accelerates bacterial growth that spoils meat. Place the animal on its back, make a careful cut from the sternum to the pelvis without puncturing the intestines. A punctured gut contaminates the body cavity with bacteria.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Beginner_P3: Remove the organs as a complete unit by cutting the connective tissue that holds them to the body wall. The heart, liver, and kidneys are edible and nutritious — set them aside. The stomach, intestines, and bladder should be removed intact and discarded away from your processing area.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Beginner_P4: Clean the body cavity with clean water and allow it to cool. Hanging the carcass from a tree branch or frame lets gravity drain remaining blood and allows air to circulate, cooling the meat faster. In warm weather, this step is urgent — meat begins spoiling within hours at room temperature.

UI_Lesson_Butchering_Intermediate_P1: Once field dressed, the carcass needs to be broken into manageable cuts. Understanding the anatomy lets you separate meat along natural seams for maximum usable yield.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Intermediate_P2: Start by removing the hide. Make cuts along the inside of each leg and peel the skin away from the meat using your knife and fist. Work slowly — rushing tears the hide (reducing its value for leather) and leaves fat and meat attached to the skin instead of the carcass.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Intermediate_P3: Quarter the carcass by splitting it down the spine and separating front quarters from hind quarters at the last rib. Each quarter is then broken into primal cuts: shoulders, ribs, loins, and legs. Follow the natural muscle seams — the connective tissue between muscle groups shows you exactly where to cut.
UI_Lesson_Butchering_Intermediate_P4: A sharp knife is the most important tool. Dull blades require more force, leading to ragged cuts and greater risk of slipping. Use a sturdy skinning knife for hide removal and a thinner boning knife for separating meat from bone. Sharpen frequently during the process — animal fat coats the edge and reduces effectiveness.

UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Advanced_P1: Advanced carpentry moves beyond raw construction into precision joinery and furniture building. These techniques create stronger, more durable connections that don't rely solely on nails and screws.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Advanced_P2: Mortise and tenon joints are among the oldest and strongest wood joints. A rectangular hole (mortise) is cut into one piece, and a matching projection (tenon) is shaped on the other. When fitted together, the joint resists pulling apart and can bear significant weight — even without glue or fasteners.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Advanced_P3: Dovetail joints interlock two pieces with fan-shaped fingers that resist being pulled apart in one direction. They are commonly used in drawer construction and box building. While time-consuming to cut by hand, dovetails create extremely strong corners.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Advanced_P4: Furniture building combines these joints with careful measurement and finishing. A well-built table or chair can last generations. Sand all surfaces smooth, ease sharp edges, and apply a finish — oil, wax, or varnish — to protect the wood from moisture and wear.

UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Beginner_P1: Carpentry is one of the most essential survival skills. Wood is abundant, renewable, and versatile. With basic tools and knowledge, you can build shelters, furniture, barricades, and storage — everything needed to establish a safe base of operations.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Beginner_P2: The most important tools for a beginning carpenter are a hammer, a saw, and nails. A hammer drives nails and can also be used to pry boards apart for salvage. A saw cuts planks from logs and trims lumber to size. Nails join pieces together. Without these three basics, carpentry is nearly impossible.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Beginner_P3: Start with simple projects: barricading windows, building crates for storage, and constructing basic wooden walls. These teach fundamental skills like measuring, cutting straight lines, and joining pieces securely. Every failed attempt teaches something — wood is forgiving enough to practice on without wasting valuable resources.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Beginner_P4: Always work on a stable surface and keep your tools maintained. A dull saw tears wood instead of cutting it cleanly, and a loose hammer head is dangerous. Store lumber off the ground to prevent rot and warping.

UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Intermediate_P1: With basic skills mastered, you can tackle larger projects: walls, floors, stairs, and roofing. Structural carpentry requires understanding how weight is distributed and how to build frames that won't collapse.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Intermediate_P2: A wall frame starts with vertical studs spaced evenly, connected by horizontal plates at top and bottom. The studs bear the weight while the plates distribute it evenly. For a standard wall, studs should be placed roughly every 16 inches. Closer spacing means stronger walls but uses more lumber.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Intermediate_P3: Floor construction follows similar principles. Joists run parallel across the span, supported at each end by bearing walls or beams. The longer the span, the larger the joists need to be. A floor that bounces when you walk on it has joists that are too small or spaced too far apart.
UI_Lesson_Carpentry_Intermediate_P4: Roofing protects everything below from weather. Even a simple shed roof — a single sloped surface — requires rafters, sheathing, and some form of waterproofing. Tarps, sheet metal, or even layered bark can serve as roofing material when conventional shingles aren't available.

UI_Lesson_Carving_Advanced_P1: Advanced carving combines artistic skill with structural engineering to create complex items: bowls, containers, furniture components, and decorative pieces.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Advanced_P2: Bowl carving starts with a section of log split in half. The bowl is hollowed from the flat face using a gouge or curved knife. Wall thickness should be uniform — thick spots dry at different rates than thin spots, causing cracks. Leave the walls thicker than you want, then finish to final thickness after drying.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Advanced_P3: Interlocking carved joints create strong connections without nails or glue. The key is precision — each piece must fit its partner exactly. Sand or file mating surfaces for the tightest possible fit. A well-fitted carved joint gets tighter as the wood dries and shrinks.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Advanced_P4: Finishing carved items improves both appearance and durability. Sanding progresses through increasingly fine grits. Applying oil (linseed, walnut, or mineral oil) penetrates the wood and protects against moisture. For food-contact items like bowls and utensils, use only food-safe oils.

UI_Lesson_Carving_Beginner_P1: Carving transforms raw wood into functional tools, handles, utensils, and decorative items using only a knife or chisel.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Beginner_P2: A sharp knife is the essential carving tool. Carve away from your body with controlled strokes. Green (freshly cut) wood is softer and easier to carve than seasoned wood, but it shrinks and may crack as it dries. Softwoods like pine carve easily but lack durability. Hardwoods like oak are tougher to carve but make stronger finished items.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Beginner_P3: Start with simple projects: a spoon, a spatula, or a tent peg. Rough out the basic shape first by removing large chunks, then refine the details with smaller, more precise cuts. Always cut with the grain of the wood, not against it — cutting against the grain causes the wood to split unpredictably.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Beginner_P4: Maintain your knife obsessively. A dull blade requires more force, which reduces control and increases the chance of the blade slipping. Strop the blade on leather frequently during carving to maintain the edge between sharpenings.

UI_Lesson_Carving_Intermediate_P2: A tool handle must fit both the tool head and the user's hand. The cross-section should be oval, not round — an oval grip prevents the tool from rotating in your hand during use. The length should suit the tool's purpose: short for hammers, long for axes.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Intermediate_P3: Fitting a handle to a tool head requires a tight joint. Carve the handle end slightly oversized, then gradually pare it down until it fits snugly. A wedge driven into a saw cut at the top of the handle expands the wood inside the socket, locking it in place.
UI_Lesson_Carving_Intermediate_P4: Spear and arrow shafts require straight-grained wood with no knots. Green shoots can be straightened by heating over a fire and bending, then holding until cool. The shaft must be balanced — an unbalanced projectile tumbles in flight instead of flying true.

UI_Lesson_Cooking_Advanced_P1: With a solid foundation in safety and preservation, you are ready to learn advanced cooking techniques. These methods allow you to create more nutritious and satisfying meals from the limited ingredients available in a survival environment.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Advanced_P2: Stewing is one of the most efficient cooking methods for survival. By simmering ingredients in water or broth for an extended period, you extract maximum nutrition from tough cuts of meat and fibrous vegetables. Stews also allow you to combine many small ingredients that would be unsatisfying on their own into a complete meal. The liquid retains vitamins and minerals that would otherwise be lost through other cooking methods like grilling.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Advanced_P3: Baking requires more infrastructure — specifically a working oven — but opens up possibilities like bread, pies, and casseroles. Bread is particularly valuable because flour stores for a long time and a single batch of dough can feed several people. The basic ratio is roughly three parts flour to one part water, with yeast or a sourdough starter to make the dough rise.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Advanced_P4: Finally, understanding how to combine herbs and spices transforms bland survival food into something worth looking forward to. Rosemary pairs well with roasted meats. Basil brightens tomato dishes. Salt is the most important seasoning — it enhances every other flavor and is itself a preservation agent. Even in dire circumstances, a well-seasoned meal boosts morale and provides the psychological comfort needed to keep going.

UI_Lesson_Cooking_Beginner_P1: Welcome to your first lesson in kitchen safety. In a survival situation, the kitchen becomes one of the most important rooms in any shelter. Understanding how to safely handle food can mean the difference between a nourishing meal and a dangerous case of food poisoning.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Beginner_P2: The most critical rule is to always check food for spoilage before consuming it. Rotten food harbors dangerous bacteria that can cause severe illness. Look for discoloration, unusual odors, and slimy textures. When in doubt, throw it out. Canned goods are generally safe as long as the can is not bulging, dented, or rusted through.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Beginner_P3: Cooking food thoroughly kills most harmful bacteria. Raw meat, fish, and eggs should never be eaten uncooked. Use a campfire, oven, or barbecue to cook food until it is no longer pink or translucent. Boiling water for at least one minute makes it safe to drink, which is essential when municipal water systems are no longer operational.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Beginner_P4: Finally, keep your cooking area clean. Wash utensils between uses, especially after handling raw meat. Store perishable ingredients in a working refrigerator or freezer whenever possible. If power is unavailable, consume perishable food quickly or learn preservation techniques like drying and smoking.

UI_Lesson_Cooking_Intermediate_P1: Now that you understand basic food safety, it is time to learn about preserving food for the long term. In a world without reliable supply chains, the ability to store food safely for weeks or months becomes a critical survival skill.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Intermediate_P2: Drying is one of the oldest preservation methods. Removing moisture from food inhibits bacterial growth. Meat can be cut into thin strips and dried into jerky over low heat. Fruits and vegetables can be sun-dried or oven-dried. Properly dried foods can last for months when stored in airtight containers away from moisture.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Intermediate_P3: Smoking serves a dual purpose: the heat helps dry the food while compounds in the smoke act as natural preservatives and add flavor. A simple smoker can be constructed from a metal barrel or even a large metal trash can. Hardwoods like hickory and oak produce the best results. Avoid softwoods like pine, as their resin produces toxic fumes and an unpleasant taste.
UI_Lesson_Cooking_Intermediate_P4: Understanding nutrition is equally important. The human body needs a balance of proteins, carbohydrates, and fats to function. Proteins from meat, fish, and beans repair muscle tissue. Carbohydrates from grains, fruits, and vegetables provide energy. Fats from oils, nuts, and animal products are calorie-dense and essential for absorbing certain vitamins. A diet lacking in any one category will eventually cause health problems.

UI_Lesson_Electrical_Advanced_P1: Advanced electrical work involves designing circuits, wiring buildings, and creating custom electrical devices. This requires understanding series versus parallel circuits and proper safety practices.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Advanced_P2: In a series circuit, components are connected end-to-end in a single loop. If one component fails, the entire circuit stops. In a parallel circuit, components are connected across the same voltage source. If one fails, the others continue working. Most building wiring uses parallel circuits so one blown light doesn't darken the whole house.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Advanced_P3: Fuses and circuit breakers protect wiring from overload. When too much current flows, a fuse melts or a breaker trips, breaking the circuit before the wiring overheats. Never bypass a fuse or breaker — it exists to prevent fires.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Advanced_P4: When wiring a room, plan your circuit layout first. Each circuit should serve a specific area or purpose. Heavy loads like heaters and refrigerators should be on dedicated circuits. Use wire nuts or terminal blocks for connections — never just twist bare wires together.

UI_Lesson_Electrical_Beginner_P1: Understanding electricity is critical for maintaining generators, wiring lights, and building electrical devices. Electricity flows through conductors like water through pipes — voltage is the pressure, current is the flow rate, and resistance is the pipe size.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Beginner_P2: The most dangerous aspect of working with electricity is the risk of shock. Even household voltages can be lethal under the right conditions. Always disconnect power before working on any circuit. Never work on wet surfaces or with wet hands. Use insulated tools when available.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Beginner_P3: A basic circuit requires a power source, conductors (wires), and a load (the device using the power). Breaking any point in this loop stops the flow of electricity — this is how switches work. Understanding this simple loop is the foundation of all electrical work.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Beginner_P4: Wire comes in different gauges (thicknesses). Thicker wire carries more current safely. Using wire that's too thin for the load causes overheating and fire risk. When salvaging wire, always check for damaged insulation that could cause short circuits.

UI_Lesson_Electrical_Intermediate_P1: In a world without grid power, generators become the primary electricity source. Understanding how to operate, maintain, and fuel them is essential for keeping lights on and refrigerators running.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Intermediate_P2: Portable generators convert fuel (gasoline or diesel) into electricity through an internal combustion engine connected to an alternator. They require regular oil changes, air filter cleaning, and spark plug maintenance. A neglected generator will fail when you need it most.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Intermediate_P3: Fuel consumption depends on load — a generator running at full capacity burns fuel much faster than one running at half load. Connect only essential devices and turn off what you don't need. A single refrigerator and a few lights uses far less fuel than trying to power an entire building.
UI_Lesson_Electrical_Intermediate_P4: Generators must be placed outdoors or in well-ventilated areas. The exhaust contains carbon monoxide, an odorless gas that is lethal in enclosed spaces. Never run a generator inside a building, garage, or basement. Position it away from windows and air intakes.

UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Advanced_P1: Advanced first aid addresses systemic illness, shock, and emergency situations that require quick, decisive action.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Advanced_P2: Shock occurs when the body can't deliver enough blood to vital organs. Signs include rapid weak pulse, pale clammy skin, confusion, and rapid breathing. Lay the patient flat, elevate their legs, keep them warm with blankets, and do not give food or drink. Shock can kill even when the original injury seems minor.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Advanced_P3: Dehydration is a slow killer. By the time you feel thirsty, you're already mildly dehydrated. Signs of severe dehydration include dark urine, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, and confusion. Treatment is gradual oral rehydration — small frequent sips of water, ideally with a pinch of salt and sugar to aid absorption.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Advanced_P4: Fever is the body's response to infection. Mild fever (up to 38.5C) actually helps fight infection and shouldn't necessarily be suppressed. High fever (above 39.5C) requires cooling: remove excess clothing, apply cool damp cloths to the forehead, neck, and armpits, and push fluids. Willow bark tea can help reduce fever if medications are unavailable.

UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Beginner_P1: Proper wound care prevents infection, which in a survival situation can be more dangerous than the original injury. Clean supplies and basic technique save lives.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Beginner_P2: The first priority with any wound is to stop the bleeding. Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth and hold firmly. Elevate the injured area above the heart if possible. Most bleeding stops within 5 to 10 minutes of steady pressure. Do not keep lifting the cloth to check — this disturbs forming clots.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Beginner_P3: Once bleeding is controlled, clean the wound thoroughly with clean water. Remove any visible debris. Apply an antiseptic if available — alcohol, iodine, or even honey (which has natural antibacterial properties). Cover with a sterile bandage.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Beginner_P4: Watch for signs of infection in the following days: increasing redness, swelling, warmth, red streaks extending from the wound, pus, or fever. Infected wounds need more aggressive cleaning and may require antibiotics. An untreated infection can become sepsis — a life-threatening systemic response.

UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Intermediate_P1: Bone and joint injuries are common in survival situations. Proper immobilization prevents further damage and allows natural healing.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Intermediate_P2: A fracture (broken bone) presents with severe pain, swelling, deformity, and inability to use the limb. Do not attempt to realign a broken bone unless trained. The immediate treatment is immobilization: splint the limb in the position you find it, padding well to prevent pressure sores.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Intermediate_P3: A splint can be made from any rigid material: sticks, boards, rolled newspapers, or even a tightly folded blanket. The splint must extend past the joints above and below the fracture. Secure with strips of cloth but not so tightly that circulation is cut off — check fingers or toes for color, warmth, and sensation.
UI_Lesson_FirstAid_Intermediate_P4: Sprains are stretched or torn ligaments at a joint. Treatment follows RICE: Rest the joint, Ice (or cold compress) to reduce swelling, Compression with a wrap, and Elevation above the heart. Most mild sprains heal in one to three weeks with proper care.
