UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_accessibilit: If the option above is enabled, this determines how many seconds a message will be visible before it begins the process of fadeout. Fadeout speed is naturally determined by your framerate.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_alwaysTellMy: If this option is selected, your player will use SayShout instead of Say to communicate changes they trigger on a jukebox; this will cause them to tell other players on a server what they have done (so that others will see above your head that you have skipped a track, picked a track, or queued something).  When this option is selected, the interacting player will always speak after successfully triggering an event on a jukebox, even if you enable Accessible Jukebox Feedback below.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_blockTrueMus: Are you on a popular server that now runs True Music Jukebox, wishing you didn't occasionally stutter when your friend's nearby jukebox begins their favorite 12-minute track from your server's enormous collection? Or perhaps you're about to run a life-or-death mission in which stuttering however briefly feels like it's not a risk worth taking? Well, this setting is for you. Enabling this will cause the play() function of this mod to be skipped for you. It will also prevent you from triggering any updates on any jukeboxes except those you pointlessly choose to activate manually (and you still won't hear any music). Any currently playing sounds will finish playing if you want to start a track and then enable this to prevent surprises. You're welcome. <RGB:1.0,0.3,0.3>  <LINE> This will prevent you from knowing when a local jukebox may be attracting zombies. You have been warned!
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_considerDist: If this option is enabled, tracks will NOT start UNLESS you are close enough to hear them. This reduces the frequency of stuttering associated with playing large sound files. OVERRIDES SERVER SETTING.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_dancingComes: If this feature is enabled and the player is not currently interacting with a jukebox, the Dance function added by this mod will appear at or near the top of the context menu. The True Music Jukebox trigger for Lifestyle: Hobbies dancing is labeled with the silhouette of a dancer if icons are enabled.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_feedbackAcce: If the text above a player's head is too small for you to read, you may enable this option to display feedback in an alternative pop-up that automatically fades out. This hides the normal Say text unless you enable Always Tell My Friends.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_hideMenuIcon: Enable this option to hide the icons that appear in the context menu when you interact with jukeboxes or their portable access keys.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_hideTracklis: Hides the context menu categories for playing and queueing tracks, which can still be done from the loot panel of your inventory UI. This menu can get pretty laggy when too many options need to be added, so this may help performance for some people.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_hideTransfer: Hide the submenus of the inventory context menu that enable transferring True Music tracks in bulk. These submenus can be used to rapidly store and retrieve True Music tracks. Options exist for moving all playable True Music tracks, moving all extra copies of True Music tracks that are found in a source container, and moving one copy of every True Music track that is not found in a destination container. These submenus only appear when interacting with True Music content.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_ignoreDistan: If this option is enabled, tracks will begin no matter how far players are from their source in order to maximize sync between all clients at all times. However, due to how Zomboid handles the creation of sound, clients may briefly stutter when tracks start. If you disable this option, clients may not sync with jukeboxes when all local players are outside of their audible range, reducing the frequency of this stutter. OVERRIDES SERVER SETTING.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_invertToggle: When menu options are used to toggle a setting on or off (rather than triggering a one-time action), their icons will show the current state of the setting by default. If you would instead like these icons to show you what the state of the setting will become AFTER you press the button, enable this option.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_mainVolumeBo: Adjusts the volume of all jukeboxes on this client. This is intended as an accessibility setting for the hearing impaired and is not recommended for most normal users (unless you REALLY like to rock out). The default setting (0) will not adjust Main Volume at all.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_mainVolume_t: Adjusts the volume of all jukeboxes on this client. Can be used to mute all audio from True Music Jukebox if it is distracting or undesirable to individual players for any reason. (Ambient volume still influences jukebox volume. Ambient volume can be adjusted in the SOUND tab of Game Options.)
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_requireMusic: If this feature is enabled, the Lifestyle dancing option will be hidden whenever you cannot hear music from True Music Jukebox.
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_showEveryTra: Show Every Track In Jukebox Playlist

Shows every track in the Jukebox Playlist submenu of the world context menu. By default, the context menu only shows the nearest 50 tracks, because hundreds of tracks will cause the menu to lag for several seconds, even on a great computer. You may remove this limit if you want to challenge both Project Zomboid and your computer.
Show Every Track In Jukebox Queue

Shows every track in the Jukebox Queue submenu of all relevant context menus. By default, the context menu only shows the first 30 tracks of the queue, because hundreds of tracks will cause the menu to lag for several seconds, even on a great computer. You may remove this limit if you want to challenge both Project Zomboid and your computer.
Show Every Track in Portable Playlist

Shows every track in the Portable Jukebox Keys menu of your key ring IFF access to that menu has been enabled by your server host. This will likely cause a moment of stutter when you click on your key ring if you are connected to jukeboxes that have hundreds of loaded tracks, but you will be able to access ALL of a jukebox's loaded tracks remotely (instead of a subset of them).
UI_TrueMusicJukebox_options_threeDimensi: By default, this mod does not apply the multidirectional properties of 3D audio that some mods use. For some users, 3D audio too heavily favors the left or right ear, and is therefore undesirable; for others, it feels more realistic. Select this option to enable it if you want to try it; to revert once you realize 3D audio is not great in Zomboid, you must skip the current track after disabling again. NOTE: Your server host has the ability to force the use of 3D sound in this mod; if your server is forcing 3D audio, this option does nothing.

UI_profdesc_YumiAfricanLion: A bold pride-born survivor with pack instincts, strength, and fearless predator confidence.
UI_profdesc_YumiAlaskanWolf: A pack-minded wolf survivor with sharp senses, strong instincts, and a hunter's patience.
UI_profdesc_YumiAmurLeopard: A stealthy night predator with padded feet, sharp claws, and silent movement.
UI_profdesc_YumiClydesdaleHorse: A powerful running survivor with heavy stamina, thick resilience, and serious sprinting talent.
UI_profdesc_YumiCottontailRabbit: A nervous but quick-footed survivor made for sprinting, dodging, and escaping danger.
UI_profdesc_YumiDomesticLonghair: A graceful night-eyed feline with soft paws, quiet movement, and elegant survival instincts.
UI_profdesc_YumiDomesticShorthair: A quick, balanced housecat survivor with nimble movement, padded feet, and fast reactions.
UI_profdesc_YumiDragon: A fire-scaled apex survivor with bite power, combat instincts, strength, and heat-resistant scales.
UI_profdesc_YumiEastAfricanCheetah: A fast-moving sprinter built for speed, reflexes, nimble movement, and hit-and-run survival.
UI_profdesc_YumiGoldenRetriever: A loyal companion type with brave instincts, helpful survival skills, and pack-bonded warmth.
UI_profdesc_YumiGreenIguana: A sun-loving reptile survivor with scales, balance, outdoor skill, and cold-blooded drawbacks.
UI_profdesc_YumiKomodoDragon: A dangerous scavenger-predator with reptile stomach, bite force, and ruthless hunting instincts.
UI_profdesc_YumiLabradorRetriever: A loyal tracker with a strong nose, outdoor skill, courage, and natural foraging ability.
UI_profdesc_YumiMixedBreed: A charming mix of instincts, loyalty, balance, senses, and adaptable survival talent.
UI_profdesc_YumiNileCrocodile: A heavy reptile predator with scaled skin, bite power, strength, and survival patience.
UI_profdesc_YumiRedFox: A clever fox built for quiet steps, scavenging, trapping, and slipping away before trouble catches up.
UI_profdesc_YumiSaintBernard: A sturdy rescue-hearted survivor with thick fur, resilience, strength, and first-aid talent.
UI_profdesc_YumiSiberianTiger: A powerful predator with claws, jaws, courage, and brutal close-combat instincts.
UI_profdesc_YumiTexasLonghornBull: A muscular horned powerhouse with territorial instincts, strength, courage, and blunt-force attitude.
UI_profdesc_YumiWhiteTailedBuck: A cautious forest survivor with fast legs, alert ears, and outdoor instincts.
UI_profdesc_YumiWhiteTailedDoe: A graceful prey survivor with sharp senses, quiet movement, and strong foraging skill.
UI_trait_YumiAnimalInstinctsDesc: Better awareness, survival instincts, and panic recovery.
UI_trait_YumiBorntoRunDesc: Massive sprinting talent with faster hunger, thirst, and endurance drain.
UI_trait_YumiCarnivoreDesc: You crave meat, fish, and eggs. Eating fruits, vegetables, or mushrooms makes you unhappy, bored, and can hurt your health.
UI_trait_YumiColdBloodedDesc: You struggle in cold weather but handle heat better.
UI_trait_YumiDigitigradeLegsDesc: Better sprinting and nimble movement, but higher endurance drain.
UI_trait_YumiFireResistantScalesDesc: Reduced fire and burn danger, but you are not immune to fire.
UI_trait_YumiHerbivoreDesc: You crave fruits, vegetables, and mushrooms. Eating meat, fish, or eggs makes you unhappy, bored, and can hurt your health.
UI_trait_YumiHornedPowerDesc: Heavy horns and raw force improve shove power, blunt fighting, and combat confidence.
UI_trait_YumiLoneBeastDesc: Better alone, worse around groups of survivors.
UI_trait_YumiNightEyesDesc: Your eyes are naturally adapted to darkness, making it easier to see and move at night.
UI_trait_YumiPackBondedDesc: Less stress and panic near allies, but worse when alone.
UI_trait_YumiPowerfulBiteDesc: A strong reptile or predator bite instinct improves close-combat survival.
UI_trait_YumiPowerfulJawsDesc: Predator-style survival trait with stronger close-combat instincts.
UI_trait_YumiPredatorsAppetiteDesc: Your body burns through food and water much faster, but your constant eating has made you naturally stronger.
UI_trait_YumiPreyReflexesDesc: Faster movement and reaction, but panic rises easier.
UI_trait_YumiPrimalFearResponseDesc: Panic rises faster, but it fits prey-animal survival instincts.
UI_trait_YumiReptileStomachDesc: Less likely to get sick from questionable animal protein, but this does not protect you from the Knox Infection.
UI_trait_YumiScaledSkinDesc: Tougher scaled skin gives a little extra survival toughness, but it is not armor.
UI_trait_YumiSensitiveTailDesc: More pain and stress when injured.
UI_trait_YumiSharpSensesDesc: Better foraging, tracking, and general awareness.
UI_trait_YumiSmallGameEaterDesc: You are built for eating small game, fish, eggs, and lean animal protein.
UI_trait_YumiSunBaskingDesc: Warm daylight calms you and helps you recover fatigue slightly while outdoors.
UI_trait_YumiTailBalanceDesc: Better balance, nimble movement, and lightfoot movement.
UI_trait_YumiTerritorialDesc: Less stress and panic around your base or familiar safehouse areas.
UI_trait_YumiThickFurDesc: Better cold resistance, but worse heat tolerance.
UI_trait_YumiThinFurDesc: Better heat tolerance, but worse cold resistance.
UI_trait_YumiWildAppetiteDesc: Hunger drains faster and you need more food.
UI_trait_YumiWildResilienceDesc: Your anthro biology is naturally tougher against normal sickness, but this does not protect you from the Knox Infection.

I tried to tell people. I tried to say, listen closer, listen between the static and the official statements, listen in the pauses where dead air isn't quite dead. They looked at me the way people look at the feverish. They stepped back. They took my batteries for their own radios and left me with the one that couldn't tune to anything but that station, that voice, that second frequency that wasn't on the dial but was in the air anyway, always in the air, waiting for ears that could hear it.

The courthouse is still there. I saw it yesterday, or what passes for yesterday when time has stopped behaving properly. The green fire is out but the building is intact, which is wrong. UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideSno:
The snowplow made it farther than the convoy. It shoved cars, luggage, and bad decisions into the ditch until the fuel died near {{noun}}. After that, winter took the road back one inch at a time.

{{openerName}} gets the useful pieces: {{skillName}} for the body, {{recipeName}} for the pot, and {{traitName}} for whatever stubborn part refuses to lie down.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideSou:
The soup kitchen kept ladling until the pot was mostly water and hope, until the ladle scraped the bottom and the sound was loud enough to make people nervous, to make them look at the door, to make them remember that hunger makes the living dangerous too, not just the dead. People said thank you like manners could keep the fever out, like please and thank you were antibodies, like gratitude was a form of PPE that you could wear over your face instead of a mask that had already been worn by someone else and never properly cleaned.

{{authorName}} wrote names on cups so the living could feel counted, so they could hold something with their identity on it even when the soup was thin and the bread was the kind that gets harder instead of softer when it sits out. The cups were from a donation drive last year, branded with a church logo and a slogan about salvation. The irony was noted but not discussed. Discussion was for people who had calories to spare on talking.

For {{openerName}}, these pages are hot soup in paper form: {{skillNameA}} first, because the body needs to be capable before the mind can be useful. {{recipeName}} second, because the mind needs to know how to feed the body even when the church donations stop and the cups run out and the only thing left is what you can make yourself from what's left in the pantries of people who don't need pantries anymore. {{traitName}} third, because surviving the holidays still counts as a miracle even when the angels are all dead and the herald angels aren't singing anything except the emergency broadcast on a loop.

If you can carry {{traitName}} without spilling it, without letting it leak out and make you vulnerable, without letting it become a burden that slows you down when you need to move - carry it. If you can't, leave it here with the cups and the names and the thin soup. Some gifts are too heavy for some people. That's not failure. That's just physics. That's just the reality of what you can hold versus what the world keeps piling on. Take what you can. Leave what you must. Keep moving. That's the gift that matters: motion, continuation, the refusal to become part of the scenery, the scenery that is increasingly full of things that don't move except to chase things that do.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideToy:
The toy store was untouched because nobody wanted to admit children still existed. We took batteries, blankets, and one stuffed rabbit that smelled like smoke. {{noun}} {{verb}} in the back room and every music box started at once.

{{openerName}} can have the notes on {{entryNameA}} and {{entryNameB}}. Leave the toys unless you need something soft enough to remember mercy.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideTre:
The tree farm smelled so normal it hurt. Pine, mud, gasoline, and somebody's old thermos coffee. We cut branches for camouflage and pretended the wreaths on the office door were not covering bullet holes.

{{survivorName}} left {{supplyNoun}} there for strangers. I left {{entryNameA}} and {{entryNameB}} for the same reason. If {{openerName}} hears bells in the rows, do not follow them.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideWar: This was wrapped for {{openerName}} with one last bit of {{adjective}} mercy. Keep {{supplyNoun}} close and make it through the week. {{exclamation}}.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideWor:
The workshop is not at the North Pole this year. It is any garage with a locked door, any kitchen with a sharp knife, any clinic with one clean bandage left. Good people make gifts out of whatever keeps someone breathing.

So here: {{entryNameA}}, {{entryNameB}}, and a little note saying {{exclamation}}. {{openerName}} can decide which part is festive.

UI_BN_Quest_antibiotics_desc: I want to understand how this thing really spreads. Bring me {count} courses of antibiotics for the research -- and I'll teach you a thing or two about patching people up.
UI_BN_Quest_antibiotics_success: "Fascinating, and horrifying. Here -- let me show you what I've learned."
UI_BN_Quest_cigs_desc: I'd trade an arm for a smoke. Bring me {count} packs and I'm yours.
UI_BN_Quest_doll_desc: If you ever come across a little doll out there... I lost my daughter's when we ran. I'd just like to hold one again.
UI_BN_Quest_doll_success: "...yeah. That's the one. Thank you. I won't forget this."
UI_BN_Quest_drink_desc: Find me a bottle of something strong. Just one. Helps me sleep without the dreams.
UI_BN_Quest_drink_success: "...I'll make it last. Probably won't. Thanks."
UI_BN_Quest_escrap_desc: Get me {count} bits of electronic scrap and I'll show you how to keep the lights on after everyone else is in the dark.
UI_BN_Quest_escrap_success: "See? Power's just patience and not electrocuting yourself. Your turn."
UI_BN_Quest_fuel_desc: There's a place I keep dreaming about -- the dark down past the warehouses. I'm not ready to go back. Bring me a can of fuel and I'll tell you what I saw there. Take this torch; you'll want it.
UI_BN_Quest_fuel_success: "...the doors were chained from the inside. Whatever did that wasn't trying to keep things OUT."
UI_BN_Quest_games_desc: Stupid thing to miss, but I'd kill to play something again. Find me {count} old video games? Even if there's no power to run them yet.
UI_BN_Quest_games_success: "Ha! Look at that. Maybe one day we hook up a generator and a TV. Deal?"
UI_BN_Quest_generic_hunt: Thin the herd -- take down {count} zombies.
UI_BN_Quest_hunt_desc: I keep hearing them at night. Thin the herd for me -- {count} of them -- and I'll sleep a little easier.
UI_BN_Quest_hunt_success: "Quieter now. Thank you. Get some rest."
UI_BN_Quest_mags_desc: Anything to read would help. Bring me {count} magazines or comics and I'll be a happy idiot.
UI_BN_Quest_mags_success: "You're a lifesaver. Don't spoil the endings."
UI_BN_Quest_saucepan_desc: Find me a saucepan and I'll turn our sad cans into something that tastes like a memory. I'll teach you, too.
UI_BN_Quest_saucepan_success: "A hot meal changes everything out here. Take this pot -- and what I showed you."
UI_BN_Quest_scalpel_desc: For the next stage I need a proper scalpel. What I'm studying... it's not pretty. But it might matter. Help me and I'll pass on what I know.
UI_BN_Quest_scalpel_success: "...the things in their blood shouldn't move like that. Anyway. You earned this knowledge."
UI_BN_Quest_screwdrivers_desc: Bring me {count} screwdrivers and I'll teach you how to keep a car breathing. We don't get far on foot.
UI_BN_Quest_screwdrivers_success: "Engines don't lie to you. People do. Here, this'll help you."
UI_BN_Quest_soda_desc: Bit silly, but... could you find me {count} cans of soda? I just miss the taste. Normal things, you know?
UI_BN_Quest_soda_success: "...ice cold would've been perfect. Thank you. Really."
UI_BN_Quest_soup_desc: Food's been thin. Could you bring me {count} cans of soup?

UI_BN_TopicR_ban_cook: "Find me an onion and a little heat and I'll make you forget it's the end of the world. For one plate, anyway."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_elec: "Give me a generator, some fuel, and ten minutes where nothing's trying to eat me. Hot showers again -- imagine that."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_mech_1: "You treat the clutch like it owes you money. But you keep us moving, so I'll allow it."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_mech_2: "Every time you grind the gears, a little piece of me dies. Otherwise? Not bad."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_med_1: "That scratch says otherwise. Sit. Let me look before it turns -- they ALL turn now."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_med_2: "'Fine' is what people say right before they spike a fever. Humor me and roll up your sleeve."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_recon: "Spent years where the only map was the sky and the moss on the trees. Towns turn me around. The wild never does."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_sold: "No. I don't. Some doors you don't open out here. Just know I'm good in a fight, and leave it at that."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_thief: "Ha. Relax. Old habits, sure -- but I don't steal from the people who watch my back. ...Probably."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_trap: "Rabbit, mostly. Fat one yesterday. Out here a snare line beats a gun -- quiet, and it works while you sleep."
UI_BN_TopicR_boss: "I'm not your dog. Watch your tone with me."
UI_BN_TopicR_deep: "With you? Maybe. For the first time, I think maybe."
UI_BN_TopicR_doubt: "That's rich, coming from you. Fine. Whatever you say, boss."
UI_BN_TopicR_flirt: "...I feel the same. Have for a while now."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_cold: "...wow. Noted. I'll keep my feelings to myself from now on, then. Lesson learned."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_confront_1: "...you didn't deny it. I don't know whether to be grateful you're honest or furious you did it. Both, probably."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_confront_2: "I won't ask you to choose -- the world's too small and cruel for that. Just don't make me feel like a fool."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_reassure: "...words are cheap, but I want to believe you. So don't make a liar of me. Please."
UI_BN_TopicR_joke: "Heh. That was awful. I needed it."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_cook: "Heat, timing, and never wasting a scrap. Pay attention."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_elec: "Rule one: assume every wire is live and wants you dead. Now, slowly..."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_fight: "Alright. Breathe out when you swing, don't flail, and never back into a corner. Again."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_mech: "Pop the hood. A car's just a thousand small problems that trust each other. Here."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_med: "Sit. First rule: stop the bleeding, then worry about the pain. Watch my hands."
UI_BN_TopicR_nag_1: "...wow. I'm doing my best out here, same as you."
UI_BN_TopicR_nag_2: "Charming. Want to trade packs and find out how heavy it is?"
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_close: "...about time. Don't let go, alright? Not tonight."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_fear: "Every single day. That's why I watch your back like I do. Don't you dare die on me."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_future_1: "A house with a door that locks for the right reasons. A garden. You, complaining about my cooking. That's the whole dream."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_future_2: "Quiet. Just quiet, and you next to me. I stopped wanting more than that a long time ago."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_love: "...I love you too. Saying it feels dangerous, like it can be taken away. But it's true."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_notice_1: "...I've noticed. I don't mind. Bit of warmth in all this -- I'll take it."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_notice_2: "Yeah? And here I thought I was being subtle about watching you back."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_open: "...then don't. I'm tired of pretending too. Whatever this is -- I want it."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_partner: "You and me. To the end of it. I'm not going anywhere -- you're stuck with me now."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_start: "...I was hoping you'd say that. Yes. Whatever this is -- let's find out together."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_stop: "...oh. Right. No, I get it. Friends, then -- I'd rather have that than lose you."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_dark_1: "A school. I won't describe it. Just... don't go to the one off the highway. Promise me."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_dark_2: "They move different at night. In packs. Almost like they remember how to hunt. I don't sleep much."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_farm_1: "The farms out past the treeline. Animals gone feral, fields gone wild, but a smart forager eats like a king out there."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_farm_2: "McCoy land had logging cabins with stocked larders. Far from the roads. Far from help, too."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loot_1: "Warehouses down by the river. Everyone hit the pharmacies first -- nobody thinks about the loading docks."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loot_2: "The gun store in town was stripped day one. But the houses behind it? People left in a hurry. Doors still unlocked."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loux_1: "The big city? They walled it and it didn't matter. Millions behind that concrete. If you go in, you don't come out -- but the mall never got picked clean..."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loux_2: "Louisville's a graveyard the size of a county. Army dropped the bridges to slow them. Whatever's behind the wall is still in there, pacing."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_march: "March Ridge, maybe. Small, fenced. There were army trailers parked at the south end before the end -- supplies, if the looters left any."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_mil_1: "The Knox facility up north was ground zero. Whole region got sealed off -- nobody who went to look came back."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_mil_2: "There was a checkpoint on the bridge to West Point. By the end they were turning survivors away at gunpoint."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_muld_1: "Muldraugh's a one-road town -- gas station, warehouses, a sawmill. The horde rolls down Main Street like a tide. Loot the edges, never the middle."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_muld_2: "There's a storage lot in Muldraugh nobody bothered with. Padlocks, mostly. If you've got a sledge and nerve, might be worth it."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_river: "Riverside's quieter -- rich little river town. Big houses, full pantries, folks who locked up tight and never made it back. Watch the gated streets."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_safe_1: "People whispered about a prepper's bunker out in the forest. Could be a myth -- could be the last dry bed in the county."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_safe_2: "The Rosewood fire station had a solid setup before it got overrun. Might still be worth a look, if you're brave."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_signal_1: "A looping emergency message, mostly. But one night I swear I heard a real voice -- a woman, giving coordinates. Then static. I've wondered ever since."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_signal_2: "The official channels went dead weeks ago. Anything you hear now is either a recording... or someone who shouldn't still be out there talking."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_west: "West Point's got everything and ten thousand of them to guard it. The pharmacy and the gun store are gold -- if you can stand the noise you'll make getting out."
UI_BN_Topic_ban_cook: What I'd give for a real meal.
UI_BN_Topic_ban_elec: Think you could get us some power?
UI_BN_Topic_ban_recon: You always know which way's north.
UI_BN_Topic_ban_thief: Should I be counting my supplies?
UI_BN_Topic_deep: Do you think we'll make it?
UI_BN_Topic_info: What do you know about the area?
UI_BN_Topic_intimidate: You really don't want to test me.
UI_BN_Topic_jeal_confront: I know there's someone else, isn't there?
UI_BN_Topic_jeal_reassure: You're the one I trust most. That's the truth.
UI_BN_Topic_joke: Want to hear a bad joke?
UI_BN_Topic_learn_fight: Teach me to handle myself in a fight.
UI_BN_Topic_nag: You could carry more, you know.
UI_BN_Topic_reassure: We'll make it through this. I've faced worse.
UI_BN_Topic_rom_fear: Aren't you scared of losing me out there?
UI_BN_Topic_rom_future: If the world ever settles... what would you want?
UI_BN_Topic_rom_love: I love you. I needed to say it out loud.
UI_BN_Topic_rom_notice: I catch myself watching you sometimes.
UI_BN_Topic_rom_open: I don't want to pretend this is just survival.
UI_BN_Topic_rom_partner: It's you and me. Whatever comes.
UI_BN_Topic_rom_start: I'd like us to be more than friends.
UI_BN_Topic_rom_stop: I think we work better as friends.
UI_BN_Topic_rumor_dark: What's the worst thing you've seen?
UI_BN_Topic_rumor_loot: Where would you look for supplies?
UI_BN_Topic_rumor_loux: What do you know about Louisville?
UI_BN_Topic_rumor_safe: Are there any safe places left?
UI_BN_Topic_rumor_signal: Has anyone heard a radio broadcast?
UI_BN_Topic_tease: You snore like a chainsaw, you know.

UI_EHR_Codex_LockedDesc: Read the matching disease flyer or reach First Aid level 8 to unlock symptoms, causes, prevention, and treatment notes.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Cause: Receiving blood that is incompatible with your body.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Duration: 2-4 days without treatment; can become fatal quickly.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Prevention: Use compatible blood and test compatibility whenever possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Symptoms: Lower back pain, severe weakness, nausea, high fever, hemolysis, endurance loss, and dangerous health decline.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Treatment: IV fluids and furosemide are the main treatments. Antipyretics, anti-nausea tablets, and anti-inflammatory pills reduce symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Cau: Fungal spores from decomposing corpses in damp, wet, or cold conditions.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Pre: Wear face protection near damp corpse-filled areas and avoid breathing contaminated air.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Sym: Respiratory irritation, fever, coughing, wheezing, endurance loss, and weakness.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Tre: Bronchodilator inhaler and antipyretics for symptoms; antifungal tablets or IV amphotericin to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Cause: A spreading bacterial skin infection after a poorly closed wound. Rough suturing has a high risk of starting cellulitis.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Prevention: Clean wounds before suturing, use sterile supplies, and avoid rough stitching when possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Symptoms: Hot red skin, swelling, local pain, fever, fatigue, weakness, and reduced endurance. Untreated stage 4 can progress into sepsis.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Treatment: Antibiotic ointment can treat mild cases. Prescription antibiotics, broad-spectrum antibiotics, plant-based antibiotics, IV antibiotics, or IV vancomycin treat more serious cases. Anti-inflammatory and antipyretic tablets reduce symptoms only.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Cause: Cold, wet, or prolonged exposure while exhausted.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Prevention: Stay warm, dry, rested, and protected from bad weather.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Symptoms: Coughing, sneezing, mild fever, fatigue, and reduced stamina.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Treatment: Rest, fluids, cough medicine, antipyretics for fever; Cold & Flu tablets or antiviral capsules can cure it over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Cause: A hard head impact from a height fall or serious vehicle crash.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Prevention: Avoid high falls and severe crashes. Treat head impacts as dangerous even if you can still walk.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Symptoms: Headache, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, and disorientation that gradually improves over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Treatment: No direct cure. Rest and time are the main treatment; symptom medicine can make recovery easier.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Cause: Prolonged exposure to decomposing corpses, especially in enclosed spaces.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Prevention: Ventilate corpse-filled spaces and wear effective face protection.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Symptoms: Eye irritation, nausea, dizziness, weakness, coughing, and possible collapse at high exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Treatment: Fresh air immediately. Anti-nausea tablets help symptoms; respiratory support kit or corticosteroids can treat severe cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Cause: Extreme stress held at its breaking point for many hours.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Prevention: Reduce stress before it reaches a prolonged maximum state.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Symptoms: Hallucinated sounds, irrational speech, visual distortion, and unsafe impulsive behavior.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Treatment: Antipsychotics. Requires an 8-dose course over 4 days.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Cause: Tainted water or severe gastrointestinal contamination.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Prevention: Drink clean or boiled water and avoid unsafe water sources.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Symptoms: Severe diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, fever, weakness, and possible blood loss.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Treatment: Electrolytes and anti-diarrheal medicine for symptoms; IV ciprofloxacin for severe bacterial infection.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Cause: Rotten food, burned food, or stale food.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Prevention: Eat fresh food and avoid food that has spoiled, burned badly, or gone stale.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, endurance drain, increased hunger and thirst.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Treatment: Anti-nausea tablets, electrolyte powder, and activated charcoal. Activated charcoal can cure it over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Cause: Eating with bloody or dirty hands.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Prevention: Wash hands before eating. Soap and clean water are best.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Symptoms: Severe nausea, vomiting, dehydration, stomach pain, and fatigue.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Treatment: Anti-diarrheal medicine, electrolyte powder, antiviral capsules, or IV ciprofloxacin for severe bacterial cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Cause: Heat exposure, dehydration, heavy clothing, or exertion in hot weather.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Prevention: Hydrate, rest in shade, wear lighter clothing, and avoid overexertion in heat.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Symptoms: Dizziness, nausea, weakness, thirst, fatigue, and overheating.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Treatment: Cool down, rest, drink water, and use electrolyte powder.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Cause: Extreme heat exposure or severe dehydration.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Duration: Critical until body temperature is controlled.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Incubation: Can develop from untreated heat exhaustion.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Prevention: Avoid extreme heat, hydrate aggressively, and treat heat exhaustion early.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Symptoms: Extreme body temperature, delirium, confusion, vomiting, collapse/blackouts, dehydration, and life-threatening health loss.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Treatment: Immediate cooling. Instant ice packs can cure heat stroke with a 4-dose cooling course; fluids and electrolytes help dehydration.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Caus: Prolonged exposure to contaminated dirt or grass. The first bite leaves a scratch-like wound.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Prev: Avoid lingering on bare dirt or grass when possible, cover exposed skin, and keep wounds clean.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Symp: Severe itching, repeated scratch wounds, bite-site pain, fever, and dangerous health decline in late stages.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Trea: Topical permethrin is the main treatment. Antiparasitic pills can also cure it, but the course is longer.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Cause: Low body temperature from cold, wet clothing, wind, or exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Prevention: Wear insulation, stay dry, and get indoors during severe cold.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Symptoms: Shivering, weakness, confusion, fatigue, and dangerous temperature drop.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Treatment: Warm up, change into dry clothes, rest, and use external heat sources.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Cause: Prolonged extreme fatigue, caffeine crash, combat stimulant crash, or nitric oxide booster crash.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Incubation: Triggered after 12 hours at very high fatigue, or rarely after stimulant crashes.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Prevention: Sleep before exhaustion becomes prolonged and avoid stacking strong stimulants.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Symptoms: Poor rest, inability to sleep naturally in later stages, stress, fatigue, and headache.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Treatment: Sleeping pills allow sleep while active. Dual orexin receptor medication cures over 96 hours; antidepressants cure over 168 hours.
UI_EHR_Codex_knox_infection_Symptoms: Fever, nausea, weakness, pale skin, and terminal systemic infection.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Cause: Severe or untreated respiratory illness, cold exposure, or weakened health.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Prevention: Treat respiratory illness early and avoid prolonged cold exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Symptoms: Fever, coughing, chest pain, endurance loss, and potentially lethal respiratory failure.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Treatment: Prescription or broad spectrum antibiotics cure over time; IV Ciprofloxacin is the fast clinical cure. Bronchodilator helps breathing, cough medicine suppresses coughing, antipyretics reduce fever.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Cause: Untreated severe infection entering the bloodstream.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Prevention: Treat wound infections and cellulitis before they spread.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Symptoms: High fever, extreme weakness, confusion, rapid decline, and life-threatening systemic illness.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Treatment: IV antibiotics and aggressive medical support. This is an emergency condition.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Cause: Deep contaminated puncture wounds, rusty metal injuries, or severe dirty wounds.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Prevention: Clean deep wounds quickly and use tetanus prophylaxis when possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Symptoms: Jaw stiffness, muscle spasms, pain, fever, and dangerous neuromuscular failure.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Treatment: Muscle relaxants for symptoms; tetanus antitoxin or tetanus immunoglobulin with a syringe to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Cause: Poisonous berries, poisonous mushrooms, or other toxic food.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Prevention: Avoid unidentified wild food unless you can verify it is safe.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Symptoms: Violent nausea, vomiting, dizziness, blurred vision, weakness, and dangerous systemic poisoning.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Treatment: Activated charcoal is the main treatment. Anti-nausea tablets and electrolytes help symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Cause: Raw or undercooked wild game and unsafe raw meat.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Prevention: Cook meat thoroughly, especially wild game.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Symptoms: Intense muscle pain, fever, weakness, and dangerous health loss in severe stages.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Treatment: Muscle relaxants and anti-inflammatory medicine for symptoms; antiparasitic pills or albendazole injection to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Cause: Long-term respiratory exposure in contaminated corpse-heavy environments.

UI_Manual_Chapter1_Text:
Pin tumbler mechanism is commonly used and most available mechanism for padlocks and cylinder door locks.
Main elements of pin tumbler lock mechanisms for us are driver pins, key pins and lock cylinder.
Driver pins drive key pins into the holes of the lock cylinder. Key pins are the parts that interact with any key.
When all driver pins align on the outer edge of the lock cylinder. Lock cylinder becomes unbound.
With a rotational force (for example by sturdy bent hairpin) an unbound lock opens without opposition.
Same things happen with the correct key. By putting the key in, driver pins align at the edge of the lock cylinder and the lock gets unbound.
By turning it, it unlocks. With a wrong key driver pins won't get aligned, the lock doesn't get unbind and turning the key won't be possible.
UI_Manual_Chapter1_Title: How Does Pin Tumbler Locks Work
UI_Manual_Chapter2_Text:
While a key, both align pins and apply rotational force. Lockpicking separates rotational force and pin alignment goals into different tools.
Rotation force is handled by the tension bar and pin alignment handled by the picker.
These two tools must be used together to compensate for the fact that they can't align all the pins at the same time as a key does.
Since it is hard to see small changes in tension we will use this tension meter to visualize the amount of tension applied.
When the rotational force is applied to a lock with a tension bar, pins get stuck by a particular order called binding order. The order is determined by imperfections of the lock mechanism.
Binding pin is the one that you should set other pins. This also fits the binding order as it should be.
When too much tension is applied, current binding pin will be the first one to get stuck. Stuck pins don't move.
Once enough tension is applied and the pin is lifted by picker to correct position. Pin gets set with a click sound. After this next pin in binding order, will be binding pin.
As pins get set, tension needs to be raised for the next binding pin to respond.
If tension gets too low, set pins and stuck pins will start to fall according to binding order with a click.
When all pins set the lock becomes unbound and it can be opened by further rotating the tension bar (increasing tension).
Every lock has its own binding order and it wouldn't change the second time you pick the same lock.
UI_Manual_Chapter3_Text:
Purpose of the game is opening the lock by finding the right tension range for each pin and setting them according to binding order.
Use the A and D keys to adjust tension. With a low lockpicking skill, your hands will tremble, which can subsequently lead to excessive tension. Too much tension can break your tools!
Move the mouse to lift each pin. Listen for a click when it sets correctly.
When all pins are set, you can open the lock by increasing the tension to the end.
UI_Manual_Chapter4_Text:
Security pins are made to make locks harder to manipulate with other tools than its key.
When used, security pins replace driver pins.
Mushroom pins are usually replace by first and last driver pin to make lock harder to pick.
What is special about mushroom pin is, when too much tension is used to set the pin, pin makes a false set with a click sound.
To avoid false set you need to keep tension bellow a certain amount. While this amount is always the same, it's place changes according to pin.
Another way to overcome this is keeping mushroom pin above its neck.

UI_AEP_Desc: Pick an exercise on the Fitness panel, tick AUTO and press Start. Your character will exercise, sit down to rest when tired, then get up and go again. Every setting below takes effect immediately, even mid-game.
UI_AEP_RestBelow_tt: Once endurance falls below this, the current set is cut short and your character sits on the ground.
UI_AEP_ResumeAbove: Stand back up at this endurance (%)
UI_AEP_ResumeAbove_tt: Once endurance recovers to this while resting, your character gets up and starts the next set. Keep it higher than the value above.
UI_AEP_SetMinutes_tt: How long a single set runs. It ends sooner if endurance runs out first.
UI_AEP_MoodleThreshold: Exhausted level that still allows exercise
UI_AEP_MoodleThreshold_tt: The base game refuses to exercise above this Exhausted moodle level. Set it to 4 and the moodle never gets in the way, leaving the endurance percentages above fully in charge. This also applies to the vanilla fitness panel.
UI_AEP_PainThreshold: Pain level that triggers a painkiller (0 = never)
UI_AEP_PainThreshold_tt: Once the Pain moodle reaches this level, your character reaches for pills or alcohol. Set it to 0 to disable everything pain-related.
UI_AEP_UsePills_tt: Uses painkillers (Base.Pills) from your inventory. Tried before alcohol.
UI_AEP_UseBooze_tt: Drinks a tiny amount of any alcoholic drink. The game grants the same painkiller effect no matter how much you drink, so a single sip works while barely making you drunk.
UI_AEP_BoozeSip_tt: How much to drink at a time. Less means less intoxication. Raise it a little if the sip seems to do nothing.
UI_AEP_BoozeMaxDrunk_tt: A safety cap. Alcohol is left alone once intoxication passes this.
UI_AEP_ReliefCd_tt: Keeps your character from swallowing one dose after another. Nothing is taken while a dose is still working, so this only matters when pain outlasts the effect.
UI_AEP_StopNoRelief: Stop when there is nothing to treat the pain with
UI_AEP_StopNoRelief_tt: If pain is blocking exercise and there are no pills or alcohol left, switch auto mode off rather than sitting there indefinitely.
UI_AEP_PainBlockAt: Pain level that halts exercise (0 = never)
UI_AEP_PainBlockAt_tt: At this Pain level your character stops exercising and waits for the pain to ease. Keep it higher than the painkiller level above - if it is equal or lower, exercise halts the instant your character is sore enough to want a pill. For reference, the base game locks its own Start button at level 4.
UI_AEP_MaxTries: Give up after this many doses (0 = unlimited)
UI_AEP_MaxTries_tt: If this many doses in a row fail to bring the pain down, stop auto mode instead of working through everything you are carrying.
UI_AEP_StopOnInput_tt: Switches auto mode off the moment you press a movement key, aim or attack. Only character input counts, so clicking buttons on the Fitness panel will not stop it.
UI_AEP_HeavyLoad: Heavy Load level that halts exercise (0 = ignore)
UI_AEP_HeavyLoad_tt: Carrying too much is not something resting fixes, so auto mode stops once the Heavy Load moodle reaches this level.
UI_AEP_StopZombie: Stop when a zombie is in sight
UI_AEP_StopZombie_tt: Switches auto mode off as soon as a single zombie comes into view.
UI_AEP_StopHealthMin: Health at which exercise halts (%, 0 = ignore)
UI_AEP_StopHealthMin_tt: Switches auto mode off once overall health falls below this, whatever the cause - hunger, illness or injury.
UI_AEP_StopOnDamage_tt: Switches auto mode off when health drops sharply. This catches being hit by something; slow drains like hunger are handled by the health threshold above.
UI_AEP_StopOnClose: Stop when the Fitness panel is closed
UI_AEP_StopOnClose_tt: Turn this off and auto exercise keeps running after you close the panel.
UI_AEP_KeepSpeed_tt: The game normally drops back to 1x whenever an action finishes, and auto exercise finishes an action every set, sip and sit-down. This holds the speed instead. It is released the moment things get dangerous - a zombie in sight, taking damage, catching fire - and again whenever auto mode stops. (No effect while connected to a multiplayer server - the server controls game time.)
UI_AEP_SpeedHealthMin: Health at which the speed is released (%, 0 = ignore)
UI_AEP_SpeedHealthMin_tt: Stops holding fast-forward once overall health falls below this. Meant to catch slow drains such as starvation or illness.
UI_AEP_NoticeMode_tt: Where to show what auto exercise is doing and why it stopped.
UI_AEP_StatusRepeat: Repeat the same reason every (minutes, 0 = once)
UI_AEP_StatusRepeat_tt: How often to say the reason again while your character still cannot exercise.
UI_AEP_Auto_tt: Repeat this exercise automatically, resting when needed. Tick this, then press Start below to begin.
